items.title: German police fire water cannon during tense 'Gen Z' protests
items.description: German police fired a water cannon to disperse firework-hurling protesters on Saturday and were also pelted with other projectiles, as tensions rose at the end of massive youth-led protests. In Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne and dozens of other cities, demonstrators turned out for the protests organised by the group ‘ GenZ regelt! ’ (GenZ has got this), the latest by disillusioned youth in Europe. Thousands of police were deployed across the country and, after mostly peaceful demonstrations, tensions rose in the evening in some places. In the western city of Cologne, where one of the biggest demonstrations took place, police fired a water cannon to disperse a crowd after saying protesters had targeted officers with fireworks. “We will not tolerate violence against emergency workers,” said a police statement. Protesters light dlares after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) in Frankfurt am Mian on October 31, 2026. — AFP Earlier, a march through the city was halted after demonstrators started setting off fireworks. A march was also temporarily halted in Frankfurt after protesters set off fireworks. In Berlin, protesters hurled bottles and eggs while protesters set barricades ablaze in Hamburg, and police were using pepper spray on demonstrators in some places, Germany’s daily Bild reported. Demonstrators had earlier taken to the streets waving signs that read “Time for resistance” and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. They have been inspired by similar movements across Europe, including in France and Italy . Europe-wide protests “We’re taking to the streets for a life that everyone can afford,” said Veronika Dinter, a spokeswoman for the “ GenZ regelt! ” movement. “Hardly anyone still believes in a better future if everything just continues as it is.” The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. They are also unhappy with sharply increased military spending and a new voluntary service model aimed at boosting troop numbers, fearing it is a step towards bringing back conscription. Riot Police bloct the street in front of protesters after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) in Frankfurt am Mian on October 31, 2026. — AFP Several thousand demonstrators turned out in Cologne while the figure was around 5,000 in Berlin and 8,000 in Frankfurt, according to police. There were also sizeable gatherings in other parts of the country, although the numbers were below the 170,000 nationwide that organisers had hoped for. Authorities have been worried the protests, coinciding with Halloween, could be marred by the same kind of violence seen elsewhere in Europe. Protests were also taking place in France for a third straight weekend. Nationwide demonstrations there on October 17 degenerated into some of the country’s worst rioting in years. Berlin is in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests. A policeman stands next to police cars on the sidelines of a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) in Berlin on October 31, 2026. — But prior to the protests, authorities said that they had not seen evidence of concrete plans for violence. The “ GenZ regelt! ” movement explicitly rejects violence. It stresses that “extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us — no matter from which side”. Christian Volk, an expert in protest movements, said there was the potential to see a major movement emerge in Germany. But Volk, from Berlin’s Humboldt University, told AFP there were key differences with France, which has a “completely different tradition when it comes to confrontational forms of protest”.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026, le Mali vise une première médaille
items.description: Cinq disciplines, cinq chances de briller. Le Mali prend part aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ), qui se deroulent du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026 a Dakar, au Senegal. Pour cette premiere edition organisee sur le continent africain, la delegation malienne nourrit l'espoir de decrocher au moins une medaille. La delegation compte cinq athletes, dont deux femmes. Âges de 15 a 17 ans, ces jeunes sportifs defendront les couleurs nationales en athletisme, escrime, judo, natation et taekwondo. Une delegation conduite par Abdoul Wahab Zerome, vice-president du Comite national olympique et sportif du Mali. Conscients des efforts consentis par les autorites sportives, les athletes affichent leur determination. Ils promettent de donner le meilleur d'eux-memes afin de representer dignement le Mali. Le taekwondo, un motif d'espoir pour le Mali Parmi les cinq disciplines engagees, le taekwondo suscite particulierement l'attention. Cette specialite a deja permis au Mali de signer de belles performances sur la scene internationale. Les exploits de champions comme Daba Modibo Keïta, double champion du monde, et Ismael Coulibaly continuent d'alimenter les ambitions du sport malien. La recente medaille d'or remportee par Bintou Diakite aux Championnats d'Afrique de taekwondo organises a Bamako en 2026 vient egalement renforcer ces espoirs. Reste maintenant aux jeunes athletes maliens a concretiser ces ambitions sur les differents sites de competition. a Dakar, l'objectif est clair : faire honneur au Mali et, pourquoi pas, repartir avec une medaille. L’article JOJ Dakar 2026, le Mali vise une première médaille est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Insurrection populaire et putsch manqué : Le Burkina Faso se souvient de ses héros
items.description: Le Burkina Faso a commémoré ce samedi 31 octobre 2026 les martyrs de l'insurrection populaire de 2014 et du coup d'État manqué de septembre 2015. Le président de l'Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), Dr Ousmane Bougouma, représentant le président du Faso, a présidé la cérémonie d'hommage qui s'est tenue au monument des Héros nationaux à Ouagadougou. À 10 heures précises, au pied du monument des Héros nationaux à Ouaga 2000, la sirène retentit. Par suite, une minute de silence est observée pour honorer la mémoire de tous ceux qui ont consenti le sacrifice suprême pour la liberté et la dignité du Burkina Faso. Ce moment solennel a été suivi du dépôt d'une gerbe de fleurs au pied du monument des Héros nationaux par le président de l'Assemblée législative du peuple, Dr Ousmane Bougouma. Ensuite, le président de l'ALP, les proches et les victimes se sont aussi inclinés à la mémoire des disparus. Ils ont salué le gouvernement pour avoir institué cette journée nationale d'hommage aux martyrs. « Cela fait maintenant douze bonnes années que nos parents sont tombés sous les balles assassines du pouvoir de Blaise Compaoré, les 30 et 31 octobre 2014 à Ouagadougou et dans plusieurs autres localités du pays. Pour cette 12ᵉ commémoration en leur mémoire, nous, familles des martyrs, ne saurons rester en marge et nous ne pouvons que remercier encore et encore le gouvernement d'avoir maintenu cette date de commémoration dans son agenda. Cela est à saluer à sa juste valeur et prouve que le sacrifice de nos parents tombés ne sera jamais oublié. Et nous pensons que la lutte doit continuer jusqu'à la victoire finale avec notre cher président, le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui a su prendre à temps le taureau par les cornes », a déclaré Victor Pouahoulabou, président de l'association des familles des victimes. Des membres du gouvernement et des présidents d'institution étaient présents à cette cérémonie LIRE AUSSI : Insurrection populaire d'octobre 2014 : Les héros, les désillusions et les coulisses de la bataille pour le pouvoir à la RTB Les blessés et les parents des martyrs ont été dédommagés, selon Oscibi Joanne Membre de la société civile, Oscibi Joanne fait partie des blessés du coup d'État manqué de 2015 . À l'occasion de cette cérémonie, il a rendu hommage aux disparus et salué l'initiative du gouvernement qui vise à immortaliser les martyrs de l'insurrection populaire et du coup d'État manqué du général Gilbert Diendéré en 2015. « On a vu dans ce pays les gens travailler pour tuer la mémoire de ces martyrs », a-t-il laissé entendre, traduisant sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour leur engagement à honorer les martyrs. Blessé du coup d'État manqué de 2015, Oscibi Joanne a salué les efforts du gouvernement dans leur prise en charge La victime du coup d'État manqué a également fustigé le comportement de certains acteurs de l'insurrection. « Nous étions nombreux dans la rue pour crier la patrie ou la mort. Aujourd'hui, nous sommes en révolution et quand je regarde derrière moi, il y a beaucoup de camarades que je ne vois pas. Cela m'amène à m'interroger. Souvent quand on dit la patrie ou la mort, c'est pour quelle mort ? Est-ce que c'est pour l'intérêt général ou l'intérêt singulier ? s'interroge-t-il. Toutefois, il se dit heureux parce que l'insurrection et la résistance du coup d'État de 2015 pour lui ont engendré le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Grâce au président du Faso, confie-t-il, les blessés et les parents des martyrs ont été dédommagés. « Moi qui suis de la résistance du coup d'État. Près de 95 % ont été dédommagés. Personne ne vous le dit, les gens font les choses dans le silence », a-t-il affirmé. Wilfrid Wendpanga Ouédraogo, acteur de la veille citoyenne Wilfrid Wendpanga Ouédraogo, acteur de la veille citoyenne, a salué le sacrifice des héros. Grâce à eux, souligne-t-il, le Burkina Faso est devenu un miroir pour le monde entier. Serge Ika Ki Lefaso.net

items.title: Sahara occidental : le Maroc a tout engagé, jusqu’à sa souveraineté, pour une désillusion
items.description: Tout ça pour ça. Le Maroc a tout engagé, jusqu'à sa souveraineté, pour enfin récolter un énorme désaveu sur la scène internationale. Le véto russe à la résolution américaine qui tentait d’imposer le fait accompli du plan d’autonomie marocain pour le Sahara occidental constitue une énorme désillusion pour le royaume qui a concédé en septembre dernier l'acte II des accords de normalisation avec Israël. Cela renvoie à une sentence maintes fois réitérée par la diplomatie algérienne, à savoir que nul ne peut octroyer à un pays la souveraineté qu’il n’a pas sur un territoire, fut-il la première puissance mondiale. Sahara occidental : les USA, la Russie et les faux calculs du Maroc Après avoir manigancé et gagné du temps pendant plusieurs décennies, le Maroc a cru le moment venu, en 2020, de jouer son va-tout dans le dossier en acceptant le deal proposé par un Donald Trump désireux de rallier un maximum de pays arabes et musulmans aux accords d’Abraham. Mohammed VI a misé gros. Avec une opinion publique résolument pro-palestinienne, il a pris un grand risque de déstabilisation interne, notamment après le déclenchement, qu’il n’a pas vu venir, de la guerre de Gaza. Tout au long de ces dernières années, et alors que les Palestiniens se faisaient massacrer, le Maroc s’est enfoncé dans la compromission en s’offrant entièrement à Israël via des contrats d’armement et des investissements dans divers domaines, allant jusqu'à expulser des Marocains de leurs propriétés réclamées par des revenants d’Israël. Le royaume est aussi l’un des tout premiers États à s’empresser de rejoindre, moyennant le paiement cash de 1 milliard de dollars de l'argent des Marocains, le “ conseil de paix ” que Donald Trump voulait substituer à l’ONU. Soit cette même organisation de laquelle il attendait un blanc-seing pour légaliser son occupation du Sahara occidental. Après cinq ans d’hésitation, Rabat a fini par franchir le dernier pas dans la compromission. En septembre dernier, il a été convenu avec Tel-Aviv d'élever les représentations diplomatiques respectives au rang d'ambassades avec échange d’ambassadeurs. Illusion et mensonges du Maroc sur le dossier sahraoui L'accord est survenu moins de deux mois avant le vote décisif du Conseil de sécurité sur le renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso, vendredi 30 octobre. Était-ce la condition de Trump pour appuyer une résolution plus favorable que celle de 2025 ? Quoi qu'il en soit, le Maroc a vécu toutes ces dernières années dans l’illusion. Et aussi dans le mensonge. Après l'abstention russe lors du vote de la résolution 2797 en octobre 2025, la propagande marocaine a trop vite décrété que le dossier du Sahara occidental est définitivement clos et réglé en faveur des thèses marocaines et au détriment des droits du peuple sahraoui. Sauf que, à Rabat, on a fait semblant de ne pas lire toute la teneur du texte qui n’a à aucun moment écarté l'option de l’autodétermination par référendum. C’est uniquement pour cette raison que la Russie, la Chine et même l’Algérie, qui était alors membre non-permanent du Conseil de sécurité, ne s’y sont pas opposées. La diplomatie marocaine se devait de mentir, en premier lieu à son peuple auquel il fallait montrer les “ dividendes ” de la normalisation, présentée en 2020 comme un mal nécessaire pour, précisément, appuyer les revendications marocaines sur le Sahara occidental. La Russie n’a aucune raison de laisser Washington faire cavalier seul Tout cela n’est qu'illusion comme l’ont montré le véto russe et l’abstention de la Chine vendredi au Conseil de sécurité. Non pas que Donald Trump et Israël n'ont pas tenu parole, mais parce que la diplomatie marocaine n’a pas pris en compte qu’hormis leurs alliés américain et européens, les autres grandes puissances n’ont aucune raison de froisser la légalité et le droit international. Il a échappé aux Marocains que Trump n’a pas tous les leviers, encore moins celui qui permet de changer le statut juridique d’un territoire non autonome pris en charge en tant que tel par les Nations-Unies. L’autre méprise de Rabat est d'avoir pu penser que des puissances comme la Russie et la Chine pouvaient laisser Washington faire cavalier seul et leur imposer sa volonté de manière aussi inacceptable sur un important dossier international, de surcroît dans le contexte mondial actuel. “Le don de celui qui ne possède pas à celui qui ne mérite pas” Au bout du compte, les seuls dividendes de la normalisation pour le Maroc sont que le soutien américain a entraîné celui de certains pays européens comme la France et l’Espagne. Un appui toutefois pas plus pesant que celui de Donald Trump. La vacuité de ces soutiens a été merveilleusement résumée par le chef de la diplomatie algérienne, Ahmed Attaf, lorsque Emmanuel Macron a reconnu la prétendue “ souveraineté marocaine ” sur le Sahara occidental en juillet 2024 : « C'est le don de celui qui ne possède pas à celui qui ne mérite pas… ». L’article Sahara occidental : le Maroc a tout engagé, jusqu’à sa souveraineté, pour une désillusion est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: ‘Don’t be deceived, vote for Tinubu’ – South-East govs tell Igbo
items.description: Governors of Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo States have urged the people not to be deceived by political distractions but to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The governors made the call on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East, held at Okpara Square, Enugu. The governors are Prof. Charles Soludo of Anambra, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi, Dr Peter Mbah of Enugu and Sen. Hope Uzodimma of Imo. Speaking, Mbah urged the people of the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms. He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the Federal Government’s economic reforms. The governor urged women to support Tinubu and APC candidates in the Jan. 16, 2027, and subsequent elections. “A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges. We must finish the journey we all started together,” he said. Mbah described South Easterners as strategic people who had established businesses and relationships beyond the zone, urging them to participate actively in the political process. Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-East, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women in Enugu within 48 hours. He said the beneficiaries received cash support, assistance with hospital bills and tools to enable them to generate income. According to him, the programme is designed to make women wealth creators rather than perpetual beneficiaries of financial assistance. “When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said. He urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the empowerment tools and extend the benefits to their families and communities. Uzodimma Also speaking, Uzodimma described the rally as historic and commended the First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, for empowering women across the South-East. He reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu. He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructural and economic development in the South-East. “We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said. The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the Federal Government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development. “We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said. Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers. In his remarks, Nwifuru commended the skills acquisition and empowerment initiatives of the APC-led administration, urging South-East women to vote massively for the party. He described the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development. The governor dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC. He urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the January 2027 elections and subsequent polls. Soludo Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements. He said the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the Federal Government. Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Mr Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election. Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, stressing the need for the region to strengthen its political alliances. He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet. He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges. items.title: Pakistan slams Afghan Taliban for 'shifting blame', 'persistent refusal' to address terrorism issues
items.description: The information ministry on Saturday rebuked the Afghan Taliban’s stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its “persistent refusal to address terrorism” emanating from Afghanistan’s soil. The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who blamed Islamabad’s “wrong policies” for preventing a resolution to the conflict and insisted Kabul was not the cause of counterterrorism issues. “Pakistan does not want to resolve the conflict with Afghanistan through talks,” Mujahid told Hurriyat Radio , claiming that Islamabad “lacks the necessary readiness for a peaceful resolution of differences”. In its statement, the information ministry said the Afghan spokesman’s remarks expose the “regime’s deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan”. “The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” it added. The ministry reiterated Pakistan’s “unequivocal” position: terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable.* “The Afghan Taliban regime must understand that Pakistan will not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that impact its security nor allow its people to remain targets of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” it stated. Islamabad reiterated that the “Taliban regime’s persistent refusal to address terrorism remains the principal obstacle to normal relations”. “Shifting blame, making hollow assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies will neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities. The Afghan Taliban leadership must understand that Pakistan’s security will not be held hostage to Afghan Taliban’s inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities. ” The information ministry affirmed that Pakistan reserved the right to “take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to eliminate threats to its national security, wherever they originate”. It urged Kabul to recognise that the responsibility for addressing these threats “rests squarely with the Afghan Taliban regime”. “Pakistan’s resolve to protect its people must never be mistaken for weakness,” it declared. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Multiple rounds of talks between the two sides last year, facilitated by Qatar and Turkiye , failed to bring about any workable solution, with the Pakistani government saying the Taliban officials gave no assurances on the key issues. Efforts this year made with China’s involvement also resulted in no breakthrough. September witnessed another bout of conflict between the two neighbours, with Pakistan carrying out calibrated airstrikes in the border region in response to terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This was followed by drone incursions from across the border, which Islamabad said were shot down, and two further rounds of retaliatory airstrikes. Those skirmishes continued in October, with Pakistani security forces responding to unprovoked fire from the Afghan side along the border in Kurram and Lower South Waziristan’s Angoor Adda , according to security sources. On Tuesday, Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area, which claimed the life of one local and injured a family of five.

items.title: Police repel bandits’ attack on Kebbi community
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has said that it is aware of the security incident in Ribah, Zuru Local Government Area, on 30th October 2026, when suspected bandits launched two successive attacks on the community. Police image maker, in a statement on Saturday, revealed that the first incident occurred at about 7:25 pm, when the assailants attempted to block Rambo Junction along the Ribah–Dirin Daji Road under Zuru emirate, as their attempt was promptly foiled by the joint security forces comprising the police, military and local vigilante group, who engaged them in a gun duel and dispersed them. The statement added that the attackers later regrouped and returned, shooting sporadically from different directions within the town. However, during the ensuing exchange, one Hassan Boder, aged 47, a security guard at a newly constructed filling station along Ribah–Kanya Road, was fatally hit by a bullet. Upon receipt of a distress call, the joint security team swiftly mobilised, engaged the attackers and successfully repelled them. Usman explained that security operations have since been intensified, with aggressive patrols ongoing to dominate the area and efforts underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Yes, we are aware of the attack and we have repelled it by forcing the terrorists to retreat due to superior firepower. The combined security forces have dominated the area to prevent further attacks on the communities,” he said. items.title: GPHA honours industry partners, former management at 40th anniversary awards
items.description: The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has honoured shipping lines, shipping agents, cargo customers, staff and former leaders as part of activities marking its 40th anniversary. The awards dinner recognised industry players for their performance in cargo volumes and customer service, alongside individuals whose leadership and long service contributed to the development of the Authority and Ghana’s maritime industry. Award categories included shipping lines and shipping agents by cargo volumes, roll-on/roll-off (RoRo) operations, dry bulk cargo volumes, container traffic measured in twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), outstanding customer service and top transit customers. The ceremony also recognised past Directors-General, former directors of the Tema and Takoradi ports, union chairmen, pioneering female professionals and long-serving staff. The event formed part of GPHA’s commemoration of four decades of institutional growth, industry partnership and service to Ghana’s trade and economic development. Major-General Paul Seidu Tanye‑Kulono, the Director-General of GPHA, in a welcome address, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to recognise individuals and organisations whose leadership, dedication and partnerships had helped shape the Authority. He expressed appreciation to past leaders and employees, as well as shipping lines, terminal operators, freight forwarders, transport operators, customers, and other industry partners for their contributions to the development of the ports. Mr Johnson Asiedu Nketia, the Board Chairman, in his remarks, said the awards recognised commitment, professionalism, innovation and partnership among individuals and organisations that had contributed to the growth of GPHA and the wider maritime industry. He said the Authority’s future competitiveness would depend on its ability to embrace innovation, improve operational efficiency, uphold good governance, and deliver value to customers and stakeholders. Mr Joseph Bukari Nikpe, the Minister for Transport, delivering the keynote address, called for improved port efficiency, digitalisation and stronger connections among ports, roads, railways and logistics centres to position Ghana as a leading trade and logistics gateway for West Africa. He identified six priorities for the sector: port efficiency and service excellence, digitalisation and innovation, multimodal connectivity, sustainability and safety, workforce development, and regional trade and integration. The minister said achieving these objectives required sustained cooperation among government, GPHA, private-sector operators, customers and other stakeholders across the transport and logistics value chain. He congratulated the award recipients and urged the industry to build on the Authority’s achievements through stronger partnerships, improved services and continued investment in people and technology.

items.title: Ablakwa has earned my respect – Akwatia MP vows to lead demonstration if he resigns
items.description: Member of Parliament for Akwatia, Bernard Bediako Baidoo, has thrown his support behind Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, declaring that he would personally lead a demonstration against the Minister if he resigns over allegations surrounding the distribution of financial support to Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa. He described Mr Ablakwa as one of the best public officers the country has had, arguing that the Minister had been transparent in responding to concerns about the evacuation exercise and accounting for the funds involved. His comments come after the Minority in Parliament demanded the resignation of Mr Ablakwa over claims that some Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa received less than the GH¢5,500 support package announced by the government. The demand was made by the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, at a press conference in Parliament on Tuesday, October 27. However, speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 31, Mr Baidoo questioned the basis of the Minority’s demand, insisting that the Minister had provided the necessary information when concerns were raised. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 31, Mr Baidoo rejected calls for Mr Ablakwa to step down, insisting that the Minister had earned his respect through his work in public office. READ ALSO: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments “I’ll say this today, the Honourable Okudzeto Ablakwa has really earned my respect as one of the best public officers we’ve ever had in this country. I’m telling you, and look, if he resigns, personally, I’ll lead the demonstration against him,” he said. The Akwatia MP pointed to previous instances in which the Foreign Affairs Ministry had allegedly failed to respond promptly to requests for information under the Right to Information (RTI) process, contrasting them with the Minister’s response to the latest concerns. He argued that Mr Ablakwa had made relevant information available within days of the matter being brought to his attention, suggesting that the Minister had demonstrated a willingness to account for the evacuation exercise. Mr Baidoo also questioned the Minority’s decision to focus its allegations on payments relating to the commercial flights, while making little reference to the charter flight arrangements. Turning to the Minority’s presentation of the figures, Mr Baidoo questioned the calculations used to arrive at the alleged financial discrepancies, arguing that they did not provide sufficient grounds for demanding the Minister’s resignation. He challenged the approach, describing the press conference as poorly executed and arguing that the figures presented did not, in themselves, establish that the Minister had misappropriated or failed to account for the money. “I would rather believe what the Minority has or has been saying, because they know better. But you see, when you take this presser, very unfortunately, badly done, incompetently done, I’m so shocked. If but for envy, for whatever reason, this should not come from the Minority of the Republic,” he said. He further expressed disappointment that the Minority, which he believes should understand the processes involved in demanding accountability from public officials, had handled the matter in that manner. Mr Baidoo suggested that the allegations should be examined on the basis of the information available rather than being used to push for the Minister’s resignation. He maintained that Mr Ablakwa’s response to the concerns surrounding the evacuation exercise should be taken into consideration in assessing the calls for him to leave office. Mr Baidoo, however, has dismissed the basis for the demand, arguing that the Minister’s response to the concerns raised and his willingness to provide information should be taken into consideration. The demand follows reports that at least three people contacted from the evacuation list claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the GH¢5,500 announced by the government. Meanwhile, Mr Ablakwa has denied the allegations, insisting that all Ghanaians on the evacuation list, including minors, received the full package comprising GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation.

items.title: Samson’s Take on Adu-Boahene: GHS49.1m stolen, or a story the evidence cannot sustain
items.description: The High Court on Thursday dismissed an application by lawyers for former National Signals Bureau Director General Kwabena Adu Boahene and his co-accused to strike out portions of the Attorney General’s written submissions. Any suggestion that this signals the outcome is completely ignorant commentary on the law and procedure. Justice Achibonga’s holding is essentially that a complaint about smuggling evidence or wrong attribution of testimony is immaterial because the court will only rely on the evidence on record and not merely what a lawyer says about it in his submissions. If nonexistence evidence is found out, the court will expunge it. In fact, this early stage is only for prima facie determination and not pronouncement of guilt. Remember the famous ambulance trial involving Dr Cassel, Ato Forson and Richard Jakpa. The High Court rejected their no-case submissions, but the Court of Appeal overturned that decision, acquitting and discharging them without requiring them to enter or, as we say, open their defence. That is precisely the kind of early termination the Adu Boahene defence now seeks. If they are unsuccessful, they get to make their full case in a full trial. The question at this stage is whether the prosecution has presented enough evidence to require the accused persons to defend themselves at all. After calling four witnesses, the prosecution closed its case. The defence has filed a 142-page submission of no case to answer. The Attorney General has responded in 25 pages, insisting there is a case to answer. When Attorney General Dr Dominic Ayine first announced this case, he alleged that 49.1 million Ghana cedis had been stolen through a fictitious US$7 million cybersecurity procurement. He also spoke of luxury vehicles, expensive houses and properties abroad. NewsFile examined those allegations extensively. I took some flak for appearing to defend the Attorney General’s decision to announce them publicly. My position remains: the Attorney General has a right to inform the public, but the right to announce allegations is not a license to pronounce guilt. I’m a lawyer; I know that too well. NewsFile has continued following the trial. We have even made a formal information request to ISE Holdings Limited, the Israeli company at the centre of the alleged procurement. But let’s find out why the defence believes they have no case to answer. Here are five points from their 142-page submissions. First , was the entire 49.1 million stolen? That’s a question they ask. The defence acknowledges that three cheques were issued and the money moved. But they dispute the allegation that the entire amount was dishonestly appropriated. They point to banking records and transactions involving the National Security Coordinator as they seek to discount a total of 34 million Ghana cedis. That’s nearly 70% of the 49.1 million allegedly stolen. The prosecution has the burden to satisfactorily trace these funds and establish which transactions constituted dishonest appropriation. Money moving through an account is not by itself proof of theft. The second argument important to the defence is that they ask the question: who authorised the transactions anyway, to be able to prove a crime? The defence argues that the source account was controlled by the National Security Coordinator for special security operations. They also rely on evidence that the coordinator signed or authorised the cheques. That’s the difficulty they put the prosecution in. The coordinator, at the material time, is deceased. But why were other appropriate national security officials not called to clarify the authorisation procedures and purpose of the payments? That’s a question they ask. National security cannot excuse stealing, but neither can the institutional framework be ignored when determining whether stealing occurred. Third , they ask, was the cybersecurity procurement fictitious? This was central to the Attorney General’s original public pronouncement. The defence challenges the prosecution’s account of the contracts, invoices, and alleged non-delivery. They point to documents concerning ISE Holdings Limited and argue that the prosecution has not established that the procurement was fictitious. That is why Newsfile has sought information directly from ISE Holdings Limited. Was there a genuine contract? What was paid for? What was supplied? The allegation of fictitious procurement must equally rest on evidence. Fourth , what became of the luxury properties so prominently announced? The Attorney General’s initial disclosures painted a picture of substantial personal enrichment. The defence challenges whether the prosecution has established that the identified houses, vehicles, and other assets were acquired with the allegedly stolen funds. Owning expensive property may attract the attention of law enforcement. They concede, but it does not, without more, prove that stolen money paid for those properties. Fifth, and finally , what independently establishes the criminal involvement of Adu- Boahene’s wife? The defence challenges whether the corporate relationship and financial transactions relied upon by the prosecution establish that Angela Adjei Boateng knowingly participated in the alleged crimes. Marriage is not conspiracy. Directorship is not proof of criminal intent. Proof she did any wrong. The defence shouts the law loudly. I defended the Attorney General’s right to inform the public when the case broke. I equally defend the accused person’s right to challenge the allegations and insist that the state meet its burden. Accountability demands scrutiny of both those accused of stealing public money and those entrusted with prosecuting them. So, after four witnesses, has the state established a case to answer on the alleged 49.1 million Ghana Cedi’s theft? The supposedly fictitious procurement, the disputed assets, and the criminal responsibility of each accused? While the public commentary points to holes in the prosecution’s case, the decision rests with the judge. What matters is what the evidence actually establishes, not even the dramatic announcement and confident predictions at the start of the case or what you say. Let’s never confuse the power to ….. with the proof required to convict. And that is my take.

items.description: La Société tunisienne de cardiologie et de chirurgie cardio-vasculaire (STCCCV) vient de dévoiler le programme scientifique de son congrès national, prévu du 12 au 14 novembre 2026 à Tunis. Cet événement majeur réunira durant trois jours, à l'hôtel Radisson Blu de Tunis, des spécialistes, chercheurs et experts tunisiens, maghrébins et internationaux. Dans une nite diffusée ce jour, la STCCCV précise que parmi les thématiques phares inscrites à l'ordre du jour, la question de la mort subite cardiaque occupera une place centrale, à travers des interventions consacrées aux stratégies de prévention et aux protocoles modernes de prise en charge. Ce congrès offrira une plateforme d'échange visant à promouvoir l'excellence des pratiques médicales en Tunisie et dans la région du Maghreb, affirme la même source qui a publié sur son site , m'intégralité du programme et les modalités de participation. items.title: Togo: Jah Press sacré Grand prix de l’événementiel au Sahel au SABAT 2026
items.description: Le commissaire général des Kundé, Salfo Soré dit «Jah Press» a été sacré Grand prix de l’événementiel au Sahel, lors de la quatrième édition du Sahel Business Awards au Togo (SABAT) tenue du 30 au 31 octobre 2026 à Lomé. Il a reçu son prix le vendredi 30 octobre 2026. Le promoteur culturel burkinabè, connu à l’international, Jah Press, de son nom à l’état civil Salfo Soré, vient de recevoir à Lomé, à l’occasion de la 4 e édition du Sahel Business Awards au Togo (SABAT) organisé les 30 et 31 octobre 2026, le Grand prix de l’événementiel au Sahel. Cette nouvelle distinction qui consacre le parcours d’un acteur majeur de l’industrie culturelle burkinabè et le rayonnement des Kundé dont il est le promoteur, au-delà des frontières nationales, vient confirmer davantage la stature de ce baobab du showbiz burkinabè. Cette distinction vient saluer son engagement et son parcours dans le secteur de l’événementiel, ainsi que sa contribution au développement et à la promotion des industries culturelles et créatives au Burkina Faso et dans l’espace sahélien. Pour le récipiendaire, au-delà de la reconnaissance d’un parcours individuel et de celle de l’équipe des Kundé, ce Grand Prix est également une distinction pour l’ensemble des professionnels burkinabè de la culture et de l’événementiel, dont le savoir-faire contribue à positionner le Burkina Faso sur la scène culturelle régionale et internationale. Par Wakat Séra L’article Togo: Jah Press sacré Grand prix de l’événementiel au Sahel au SABAT 2026 est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Poison in Prison; Mahama’s 3rd term; Okudzeto’s evacuees – Enimil Ashon writes
items.description: This “attempted poisoning” business at the Nsawam Prison! I am alarmed because I am concerned about the health of Chairman Wontumi. But what type of poisoning was it: food, drug, drink? Or did some inmate blow a poisoned powdered substance that went through Wontumi’s nostrils or his mouth? In the first place, does Wontumi have a cell mate? Are prisoners allowed to share food, drink, or medicines with cellmates, or anybody for that matter? The Ghana Prisons Service has, predictably, promised a “thorough” investigation. The question, however, is: what is being investigated–that someone attempted to poison Wontumi? I thought the first action by the Service should have been to prove poisoning, and what better and more convincing proof can there be than the word of a medical officer? First of all, was Wontumi rushed (sent) to the hospital? Is there a medical report? Ghana waits with bated breath for this report. Not unconnected with the poisoning issue is Wontumi’s call for prison reforms. News reports say he has begun to make interventions to improve the living conditions of inmates. It is said of Krobo Edusei, one-time Minister for the Interior in the First Republic, that having spent time at Nsawam Prisons after the 1966 coup, he told friends that had he known or been ever told about the heat in Ghanaian prisons, he, as Minister, would have installed air-conditioners in all prison cells!! Second matter arising: President Mahama and a feared third-term attempt. Are the Minority in Parliament, in particular, and the New Patriotic Party seized of facts that make the President’s word a lie?. More than once, both directly and indirectly, Mahama has given his word that a third term is not on the cards for him. For an undisclosed reason, however, the opposition is bent on letting everybody believe that they “know” the President is insincere in his protestations; that he, indeed, is eyeing a third term in office. Could it be because of the words of that Bono Region prophet whom Mahama visited recently? The TV news item reported that the prophet predicted a third term for the President. Or was it Prophet Roja’s statement on Angel FM and other platforms that he foresaw John Dramani Mahama making a comeback for a third term and claiming victory? He “prophesied” during a radio interview that John Dramani Mahama would make a comeback to run for and win a third term despite prior statements. Are these what is informing the conviction of the NPP? Haven’t we, as a people, decided to put no store by the word of these prophets, to the point of even banning them from prophesying on New Year’s Eve? Since when did Ghanaians resume trust in the word of our prophets? In July 2024, Rev. Kusi Boateng, founder of Power Chapel World Wide Church, prophesied that Dr Mahamudu Bawumia would be crowned President of Ghana in that year’s elections. To loud applause, he even predicted the exact date on which the results would be declared. Both prophecies turned out false. Rev Kusi Boateng was the former Executive Secretary of the National Cathedral Board of Trustees. Knowing some of our prophets the way Ghanaians do, it is surprising that anybody, let alone a political tradition, would doubt the word of the President (or any human being, for that matter) based on prophecies by “men of God” whom we all, as a nation, have agreed should be ignored because they are stomach-prophets. My biggest surprise is that the NPP is concerned that Mahama would attempt a third term. If the word of the opposition is to be believed, and Mahama has performed so abysmally, then there should rather be joy in the NPP camp if he “threatens” to attempt a third term. Why? Because, against such “unimpressive” performance, even a mental patient in NPP colours should win against Mahama. Third Matter Arising: Okudzeto Ablakwa versus Evacuees’ Palava. The NPP and the Minority in Parliament have questioned the disbursement of the GH¢49.72 million spent to evacuate 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa between May 27 and September 4. Among others, there have been allegations that some evacuees received less than the announced GH¢5,500 support package. At the centre of it all is the man better known to Ghanaians for his ORAL crusade. For a man who won admiration for his pursuit of righteousness over National Cathedral contracts and expenditures, the allegations are surprising, if not shocking. Some citizens are pointing out the obvious, that the Minority are pursuing an agenda against NDC who made life uncomfortable for them in government. They have made no secret of their intention not only to pay the Foreign Minister, personally, back in his own coin, but also, as a grand agenda towards 2028, to employ all the tricks deployed by the NDC while in opposition to create disaffection for Akufo-Addo’s government. I think that for Okudzeto Ablakwa, the way forward should be simple: be as transparent as possible with records regarding charter flight arrangements and expenditure.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Diamniadio, carrefour du monde à l’heure de l’Olympisme
items.description: À quelques minutes de la cérémonie d’ouverture, Diamniadio vibre déjà au rythme de l’Olympisme. « Dalen ak Diam » à Diamniadio ! Carrefour du monde, Diamniadio s’apprête à accueillir, dans moins d’une heure, la cérémonie d’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. De Dakar à Diamniadio, l’atmosphère monte. Tous les chemins mènent à Rome, dit-on. Ce soir, tous les chemins mènent à Diamniadio. À la gare, les bus attendent les spectateurs qui, après avoir marché, convergent vers le stade. Les peuples se mêlent, les langues s’entrelacent et les cultures se rencontrent. Des sourires, des échanges, une même impatience : celle de vivre ensemble, au-delà des frontières, au nom des valeurs de l’Olympisme. Moussa DIOP, à Diamniadio

items.title: Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France
items.description: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and elsewhere on Saturday as hundreds of thousands marched across France against soaring living costs and police violence, with some demonstrators dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween. While the third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests was largely peaceful, tensions erupted in several cities later Saturday. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police. At least one incendiary device was also thrown at security forces. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. “A hard core of several hundred rioters” at the rear of the march attacked police with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail, the police prefecture said. Officers were seeking “to restore public order”, it added. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators. – ‘Dressed up as angry citizen’ – Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: “No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak” and “Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween.” A protester wearing a Marie-Antoinette costume (L) holds a placard reading “Give them brioche” flanked by a protester dressed as a wizard holding a placard reading “A potion for the revolution” during a demonstration in Lyon, central-eastern France on October 31, 2026, part of nationwide demonstrations over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students. “Exceptional” security deployment with 70,000 police officers and gendarmes mobilized and an alarmist tone: for Act III of the protests against the high cost of living, right in the middle of Halloween festivities, the authorities fear a repeat of the October 17 nightmare. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) “We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice,” said Camille Guerin, 31, a demonstrator in the western city of Nantes. Authorities said that some 320,000 people rallied across France including 70,000 in Paris. According to youth organisations, nearly half a million people demonstrated across the country, including 200,000 in Paris. An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday that police had prepared for street violence on a scale “comparable” to the unrest two weeks ago, when shops were looted and public buildings set ablaze. Between 400 and 800 hard-left activists were expected in Paris, said an informed source. – Elections looming – The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen topping opinion polls. The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions. Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest. Similar youth-led demonstrations have been seen across Europe in recent weeks. Thousands of young Germans took to the streets nationwide on Saturday. In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest. “I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits,” she said. “Struggle is classy, it needs to come back into fashion.” – New school blockades – Student protesters complained the police did not authorise a march through the centre of the French capital and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week. “Starting this Tuesday, we will blockade our universities and high schools, and we will do so again on Thursday before joining the demonstration on November 5 called by workers and trade unions,” said Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union). Ahead of the protests, some shopkeepers barricaded their businesses. In eastern Paris, Wael Boubaker, a cafe employee, covered a storefront with plywood panels. “Everyone is staying home. No one is going to come and buy anything,” Boubaker said. Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who accused Macron’s government of “taking an increasingly authoritarian turn”, joined the march in Paris. With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending. Nunez said authorities had detected social media calls for Halloween gatherings on Saturday evening that urged protesters to spark a “revolution”. The post Clashes break out as hundreds of thousands protest in France appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fête de l'Unité: plusieurs projet socio-économiques inaugurés à Dakhla
items.description: Plusieurs projets à caractère économique et social ont été inaugurés, samedi à Dakhla, à l’occasion de la célébration du premier anniversaire de la Fête de l’Unité, portant notamment sur le renforcement des infrastructures commerciales et l’amélioration de la prise en charge des enfants privés de soutien familial. Inaugurés par le wali de la région Dakhla-Oued Eddahab, gouverneur de la province d’Oued Eddahab, Ali Khalil, en présence du président du Conseil régional, El Khattat Yanja, d’élus et de responsables locaux, ces projets concernent l’ouverture du sixième Village d’Enfants SOS au Maroc, premier du genre dans les provinces du Sud, ainsi que d’une nouvelle grande surface commerciale. Réalisé en 20 mois, le Village d’Enfants SOS de Dakhla comprend huit maisons familiales et quatre maisons d’accueil temporaire, avec une capacité d’accueil de plus de 100 enfants. Cette structure dispose également de plusieurs espaces éducatifs, culturels, sportifs et récréatifs, destinés à favoriser l’épanouissement des enfants et des jeunes. Dans une déclaration à la presse, le président de SOS Villages d’Enfants Maroc, Amine Demnati, a souligné que cette inauguration marque une étape importante dans le développement de l’Association et traduit sa volonté de renforcer sa présence dans les différentes régions du Royaume, en offrant aux enfants un environnement familial sécurisé et propice à leur développement. Il a également mis en avant la mobilisation des partenaires et des acteurs locaux ayant contribué à la concrétisation de ce projet. Par ailleurs, l’Association prévoit le lancement, dès 2027, d’un programme de renforcement familial au profit de 100 mères seules en situation de vulnérabilité et de 200 enfants, visant notamment à favoriser leur autonomie économique et à prévenir la séparation familiale. Sur le plan économique, il a été procédé à l’inauguration d’une grande surface commerciale, mobilisant un investissement de 180 millions de dirhams (MDH) et devant générer plus de 200 emplois directs et indirects. D’une superficie de vente de 4.500 m², cette nouvelle infrastructure propose une offre diversifiée de produits et vise à renforcer les partenariats avec les producteurs et les coopératives de la région. Le projet global, qui mobilise un investissement de 260 MDH, prévoit également la réalisation d’un espace commercial et de loisirs de plus de 12.000 m², pour un coût supplémentaire de 80 MDH, avec à la clé la création de 300 emplois directs et indirects. The post Fête de l'Unité: plusieurs projet socio-économiques inaugurés à Dakhla appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Martyrs de 2014 et 2015: le Burkina Faso s’incline devant ses héros
items.description: Le souvenir demeure, la reconnaissance reste intacte et le devoir de mémoire se perpétue. Le Burkina Faso a rendu, le samedi 31 octobre 2026, un hommage solennel aux victimes de l’insurrection populaire d’octobre 2014 et du coup d’État manqué de septembre 2015. Représentant le Chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, le président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), le camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, a présidé la cérémonie d’hommage, marquée par un profond recueillement et une vive émotion. À 10 heures précises, la sirène a retenti. Une minute de recueillement a ensuite été observée en mémoire de ces filles et fils du Burkina Faso qui ont payé de leur vie leur engagement pour la liberté, la dignité et les aspirations profondes du peuple. Le dépôt de gerbe est venu consacrer ce moment de reconnaissance nationale. Cet hommage ravive la mémoire de celles et ceux dont le sacrifice a marqué l’histoire du Burkina Faso. La cérémonie a connu la participation de députés, de membres du Gouvernement, de présidents d’institutions, de représentants du corps diplomatique ainsi que des familles des martyrs. Tous se sont réunis dans un même élan de solidarité et de recueillement pour honorer la mémoire des disparus et réaffirmer la reconnaissance de la Nation envers ceux qui ont consenti le sacrifice suprême. Se souvenir des martyrs, c’est aussi porter leur mémoire, faire vivre leurs idéaux et transmettre aux générations futures le prix de la liberté. Source : Assemblée Législative du Peuple L’article Martyrs de 2014 et 2015: le Burkina Faso s’incline devant ses héros est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Guinée : L’Association des Professionnels de la Publicité Scelle son unité et passe un cap historique
items.description: Une page décisive s’est tournée ce samedi 31 octobre 2026 pour le secteur de la communication en Guinée. Dans une ambiance empreinte de cohésion et de fierté retrouvée, l'Association des Professionnels de la Publicité (APP) a tenu sa toute première Assemblée générale au cœur de son tout nouveau siège à Kobayah. Entre réconciliation, légitimité institutionnelle et ambitions économiques nationales, la corporation a affirmé sa volonté de parler désormais d'une seule et même voix. L'événement a été marqué par une forte portée symbolique dès l'ouverture des travaux. Prenant la parole face à une assemblée attentive, Ibrahima Dieng, président sortant de l'APP Guinée, n'a pas caché son émotion face au chemin parcouru. Saluant le travail remarquable accompli par l'équipe dirigeante actuelle en un temps record, il a rappelé la vision initiale qui avait autrefois souffert de divergences idéologiques. « Le succès d'un ancien président, ce n'est pas de voir son successeur faire la même chose que lui, mais de le voir aller plus loin, » a affirmé Ibrahima Dieng, sous les applaudissements de la salle. S'adressant à ses pairs, l'ancien dirigeant a insisté sur la dimension collective de la démarche associative : « Une association n'appartient ni au président ni à son bureau, mais à l'ensemble de ses membres. N'acceptez jamais que les intérêts individuels priment sur les intérêts collectifs. Quoi que soient vos ambitions, si vous n'êtes pas unis, vous ne pourrez rien réaliser de durable. » Présentant le rapport d'activité, Alpha Barry, secrétaire général de l'APP Guinée, a dressé le bilan des avancées structurantes enregistrées par le bureau exécutif. Ces résultats concrétisent l'ancrage légal et stratégique de l'organisation dans l'écosystème économique guinéen. « La légitimité de l'APP à représenter et défendre la corporation auprès des autorités. L'acquisition du nouveau siège à Kobayah devient un symbole de stabilité, de pérennité et un espace de concertation permanente. L'adhésion à la Confédération Générale des Entreprises de Guinée (Patronat guinéen) renforce la présence du secteur dans les grands débats économique. La création du comité mixte APP-OGP (Office Guinéen de Publicité) instaure un cadre d'échange permanent pour trouver des solutions durables aux enjeux de la profession. L'APP rassemble désormais près de 40 entreprises adhérentes issues de la communication et de la publicité », a-t-il expliqué. « Derrière chaque campagne publicitaire ou chaque opération de communication, il y a des entreprises, des emplois et de la valeur ajoutée. Nous devons être fiers de notre profession et valoriser sa contribution au développement de la Guinée », a rappelé Alpha Barry. Clôturant la série d'interventions, le président entrant de l'APP, Adama Diané, a livré un discours rassembleur et résolument tourné vers l'avenir. Sans masquer le passé tumultueux de la corporation, il a appelé à transformer les divergences passées en leviers de performance collective. « Nous venons de loin. Notre profession a connu des désaccords et des divisions. La responsabilité d'un dirigeant n'est pas de masquer les difficultés, mais de travailler à les dépasser. Malgré nos différences, nous avons recommencé à nous parler, » a déclaré Adama Diané. Plaçant la défense des intérêts de la profession au cœur de sa feuille de route, le nouveau président a souligné que la publicité constitue un tremplin socio-économique essentiel pour l'effort national. Il a réaffirmé son ambition de bâtir une organisation solide, respectée et capable d’influer sur les politiques du secteur. Make vote-buying costly in party elections — Bernard Mornah
items.description: The leader of the People’s National Convention (PNC), Bernard Anbataayela Mornah, has called on political parties to make vote-buying costly, campaign financing transparent, and competence central to the selection of leaders. He said that when access to political leadership depended on who could pay the most, competence and commitment to public service risked being displaced, weakening members’ confidence that their choices mattered. Mr Mornah, in a statement, said the response must cut across all parties, adding that appeals to conscience had to be backed by rules that parties were willing and able to enforce. Ban on inducements He proposed that party rules expressly prohibit cash, goods, mobile-money transfers and payments through agents meant to influence votes. Candidates, he said, should be held accountable for inducements they authorised or knowingly financed through intermediaries, with responsibility established through evidence. Spending limits Mr Mornah called for realistic spending ceilings and a requirement that candidates declare donations, their sources and expenditure, including support in goods or services. Independent checks should be arranged and accessible summaries published, he added, noting that the Ghana Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) had also called for comprehensive political finance reform. Election day support Parties should organise modest transport and refreshments centrally, with published costs and equal treatment, he said, to reduce the chances of inducements being disguised as transport allowances. “Candidates should not give personal allowances to delegates,” he added. Candidate forums He proposed compulsory forums where contestants would explain their records, understanding of the office and practical plans. Candidates should have equal access to members through official party platforms, he said, so that personal wealth did not determine whose message was heard. Sanctions Mr Mornah called for an impartial complaints panel, confidential reporting channels, clear evidence standards and fixed decision deadlines. Proven breaches, he said, should attract proportionate sanctions, potentially including disqualification or annulment, under rules adopted in advance and subject to appeal. Lower cost of contesting He also proposed moderate nomination fees, shorter campaign periods and shared campaign platforms to help capable members without wealthy sponsors to compete. Regular membership dues, transparent fundraising and stronger political education would also reduce dependence on wealthy patrons, he said. PNC’s next step Mr Mornah said that before its next internal elections, the PNC should adopt clear safeguards through its appropriate decision-making bodies, appoint a credible enforcement committee and brief candidates and members on the rules. Every candidate should submit a campaign finance declaration, and the party should publish a financial compliance report after the elections, he added. He clarified that the measures were proposed reforms, not a statement that each was already required by Ghanaian law, and that any sanctions should be consistent with applicable law and party constitutions. “Our parties must reward service, integrity and ability,” he said.

items.title: A Pro-Russia Strongman at Mar-a-Lago
items.description: In the days after Tuesday’s midterm elections, luminaries of the MAGA movement will gather at Mar-a-Lago to turn their attention to 2028. Speakers will include a Cabinet secretary, the head of the Domestic Policy Council, and several members of Congress. Also present will be Milorad Dodik, the pro-Russia strongman who has bragged about spying on Americans and recently called Russian President Vladimir Putin “one of the most peace-loving leaders of our time.” Dodik is the de facto leader of Bosnia’s Serb population, whose push for secession risks reigniting bloody sectarian conflict in the Balkans. Dodik’s travel plans were described to me by several people familiar with them. These people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to preview nonpublic matters, said the details could change at the last minute. (His office did not respond to a request for comment.) But Dodik’s expected attendance reflects his reversal of fortune under the Trump administration, the success of a pricey foreign lobbying campaign, and a further alignment of American and Russian interests. Dodik’s government paid two of Trump’s top political advisers, James Blair and Chris LaCivita, as consultants and brought them to the Serb-majority entity for the Bosnian elections earlier this month. (They later donated their earnings to Trump’s presidential library fund after news of the work became public and the president lashed out at them on Truth Social.) When his party won a decisive result, Dodik credited both Trump and Putin for their support. “If it had not been for Donald Trump’s magnificent victory,” Dodik told supporters after the favorable result, “we would probably be political corpses today.” In 2022, the Biden administration sanctioned Dodik for what the Treasury Department called “graft,” “corruption,” and “bribery,” as well as threats to the stability of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Balkan nation where ethnic divisions catalyzed a brutal war from 1992 to 1995. The conflict climaxed in the genocide at Srebrenica, which until Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine was the most horrific mass murder in Europe since World War II. Dodik, according to the U.S. government, had attempted to sabotage the accords that ended the war, the Dayton peace agreement. He was accused of creating parallel state institutions in the federated country’s Serb-majority entity, known as Republika Srpska, and of denigrating other ethnic and religious groups, above all Muslim Bosniaks. Numerous family members, allies, and companies were eventually also sanctioned. Formerly Srpska’s president, Dodik was stripped of that position and banned from holding office for six years after being convicted by the Bosnian judicial system last year of flouting decisions by the international envoy overseeing the Dayton Accords. He has rejected those decisions as politically motivated and void of constitutional authority, and continues to exercise near-total control over Srpska’s institutions. Since Trump returned to office last year, the Srpska government has unleashed millions of dollars on lobbyists in a bid to burnish Dodik’s image with the people around Trump. The strategy has been to portray him as a martyr in the American president’s image—a victim of legal maneuvering and a crusader for Christian values holding back what some Serbian nationalists characterize as a tide of Muslim influence. Among those whose services Dodik and his allies have tapped are Rudy Giuliani, the president’s former personal lawyer; Rod Blagojevich, the former Illinois governor who landed a pardon from Trump last year; and the firm employing Katie Wiles, the daughter of White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. [ Read: The Trump family sparks a revolution in Albania ] In October 2025, the Trump administration dropped the sanctions. The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control did not offer a rationale, but the State Department had days earlier hailed several conciliatory steps taken by Srpska’s legislative body as the result of Washington’s efforts to “defuse the crisis in Bosnia and Herzegovina.” State Department officials also pushed for the resignation of the international envoy who had clashed with Dodik. Christian Schmidt, a conservative German politician who had taken up the role of high representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2021, complied in May of this year, telling a German newspaper that he had come under “enormous and unexpected pressure from the U.S.” Diplomats in the region as well as experts have viewed the Trump administration’s concessions to Dodik with significant alarm because of his avowed separatist aims and his explicit backing by Putin. Both Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina are candidates for European Union membership. The event planned for next week at Mar-a-Lago is an offshoot of the Conservative Political Action Conference, a right-wing jamboree that has enlarged its international footprint in recent years. It’s called the CPAC Circle Retreat and Gala and is billed as a “Gathering of Visionaries.” The website makes explicit the event’s connection with the next presidential election, stating, “As midterm election results come in, we’ll discuss what they mean for the political landscape and the road to 2028.” Speakers include the secretary of labor and at least two U.S. senators, Mike Lee of Utah and Rick Scott of Florida. Eduardo Bolsonaro, the brother of Flávio Bolsonaro, the failed Brazilian presidential candidate who recently arrived in the U.S. to evade possible prosecution on allegations of money laundering and tax evasion, is another advertised speaker. When I asked Matt Schlapp, the chairman of the American Conservative Union and CPAC’s host, about Dodik’s attendance, he told me, “We will have a very interesting group of donors and VIPs, but we won’t comment on who will be in attendance other than who the speakers will be.” He added that the “focus will be on America’s future heading into 2028.” It’s not clear whether Trump will be at Mar-a-Lago during Dodik’s anticipated visit, but his presence there will take him into one of MAGA’s main nerve centers. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. During a visit to Washington earlier this year, Dodik had photo ops with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Karoline Leavitt, the then–White House press secretary. Current and former U.S. officials told me that Dodik may feel pressure to achieve his aim of securing Srpska’s independence soon, given that Trump is likely to be friendlier to him than a potential Democratic successor after 2028. Tuesday’s election in the U.S. will help determine MAGA’s long-term political viability. No matter the result, Trump will have another two years to keep giving Dodik what he wants.

items.title: US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio
items.description: US President Donald Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday. “We can achieve military objectives if we seek to,” Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting. But Rubio added that Trump “hasn’t made a decision” on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday. “I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly,” Rubio said. While he slammed Tehran for “actively and openly” targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump’s preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran. But he did not commit to a timeline for talks. “I’m not going to characterize neither the progress on those talks nor any timeframe on it, other than to tell you that if there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it,” Rubio said. Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections. Trump earlier warned of the potential for fresh military action after US midterms, saying previously that he was weighing up whether to “finish them off.” But any further attack would spark concern among US allies. On Thursday, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP: “We are calling for a diplomatic solution, and really, escalation does not benefit anyone.” AFP The post US yet to decide on new Iran strikes, says Rubio appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GTEC cautions universities against compromising quality in doctoral admissions
items.description: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has cautioned universities against admitting more doctoral candidates than their institutional capacity can adequately support, warning that the practice could undermine the quality and credibility of doctoral education in the country. The Commission said the expansion of doctoral programmes must be matched by adequate numbers of qualified supervisors, research infrastructure, library resources and funding to ensure effective supervision and quality research. Professor Ahmed Abdulai Jinapor, the Director-General of GTEC, gave the warning on Saturday during the graduation ceremony of the African University of Communication and Business in Accra. A total of 350 students graduated from the University, comprising 206 undergraduates and 144 postgraduate students. The ceremony was on the theme “Transforming Higher Education for a Resilient Nation: Leveraging Technology for Sustainable Development.” He said doctoral education was critical to producing the next generation of researchers, lecturers and policy thinkers, but institutions must not allow the quest to increase enrolment to compromise academic standards. “Growth in numbers must never outpace capacity,” he stressed, adding that doctoral qualifications represented years of rigorous study, original research and examination and must not be treated as commercial products. Prof. Jinapor urged all universities, particularly newly chartered institutions, to align doctoral admissions with their actual capacity, insisting that quality rather than quantity must define doctoral education in the country. The Director-General said this against the backdrop of the institution’s attainment of chartered status, which he described as a significant milestone that brought greater academic autonomy and institutional responsibility. Touching on the theme, he said universities must rethink their teaching, research and engagement with industry to prepare graduates for an increasingly technology-driven world. He noted that artificial intelligence, automation, big data, digital platforms and cybersecurity were transforming professional and economic activities, making it imperative for higher education institutions to equip students with relevant skills. Online, blended and distance learning, he said, offered opportunities to widen access to tertiary education, particularly for working people, persons in remote communities and persons with disabilities. However, Prof. Jinapor warned that digital education must not become a shortcut to lower academic standards. He said degrees obtained through online learning must carry the same value as those awarded through traditional campus-based programmes. That, he explained, required accredited programmes, properly trained faculty, reliable digital platforms, credible assessment systems and adequate learner support. He said GTEC would continue to ensure that quality assurance mechanisms kept pace with evolving modes of educational delivery. The Professor urged the graduates to embrace lifelong learning and acquire the skills to work effectively with emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. He encouraged them to develop the ability to analyse data, distinguish credible information from misinformation and adapt to changes in their respective professions. Prof. Jinapor cautioned them against allowing technology to replace independent thinking, integrity and sound judgment. “Do not compete with technology. Learn to work intelligently with technology,” the representative advised. He said the Commission had intensified public education on recognised institutions and accredited learning centres to protect prospective students from enrolling in unrecognised institutions. He disclosed that GTEC published a notice in July 2026 concerning 15 unaccredited learning centres and institutions whose institutional accreditation had expired. The Commission also published an updated list of 110 unrecognised institutions as of September 2026, urging the public to exercise due diligence before enrolling in tertiary programmes. Ms Barbara Kafui Abram, the Overall Best Graduating Student, Faculty of Strategic Communication, encouraged the graduates to remain determined in the pursuit of their ambitions, stressing that previous academic disappointments should not define their future. She said her personal journey from an earlier unsuccessful tertiary education experience to emerging as the institution’s overall best graduating student demonstrated the importance of perseverance, determination and the courage to start again. “Never be ashamed of starting again. Starting again is not a failure. It is the courage to pursue a better ending,” she said.
