items.title: Centrafrique : Faustin-Archange Touadéra salue le soutien russe et plaide pour une place accrue de l'Afrique à l'ONU
items.description: Dans un entretien exclusif accorde a RT en francais, le president centrafricain Faustin-Archange Touadera a tenu a remercier la Russie et personnellement le president russe Vladimir Poutine pour leur soutien a Bangui durant les annees de crise. Selon lui, alors que le pays traversait une periode particulierement difficile, marquee par la presence de groupes armes et un embargo des Nations unies sur les armes, Moscou a repondu a ses sollicitations en apportant une assistance dans le domaine de la defense. « La Federation de Russie et le president Poutine sont venus aider la Republique centrafricaine a travers les specialistes russes qui etaient venus pour la formation de nos militaires, surtout sur la formation des armes que Federation de Russie a bien voulu gracieusement mettre a la disposition de nos forces de defense qui n'en avaient pas du tout », a-t-il declare. Le chef de l'etat centrafricain a souligne que cette cooperation securitaire avait constitue l'un des fondements du retour de la paix dans le pays. Il a egalement rappele que le partenariat entre Moscou et Bangui ne se limitait plus a ce domaine et entrait desormais dans une nouvelle phase, appelee a s'etendre a differents secteurs. Le president centrafricain a par ailleurs exprime sa reconnaissance pour l'aide alimentaire russe, notamment les dons de cereales qui, selon lui, ont contribue a faire baisser le prix de la farine en Centrafrique. « Cela a ete tres utile. Le peuple centrafricain est vraiment reconnaissant a la Federation de Russie, a travers le president Poutine, pour cela », a-t-il affirme. Touadera plaide pour la reforme de l'ONU afin de donner a l'Afrique la place qu'elle merite Interroge sur la possibilite de presenter un candidat africain commun au poste de secretaire general des Nations unies, le president centrafricain a indique que cette perspective correspondait aux aspirations du continent. Il a notamment insiste sur la necessite de revoir la gouvernance de l'organisation internationale, estimant que la composition actuelle de ses instances dirigeantes ne refletait plus les realites geopolitiques contemporaines. « Ce qui s'est passe en 1945, la situation a beaucoup evolue. Il faut tenir compte de cela. On ne peut pas rester dans le contexte de 1945 et gouverner l'Organisation des Nations unies comme si on etait en 1945. Nous sommes en 2026, il faut tenir compte de ces realites », a-t-il declare. Sur ce point, le dirigeant centrafricain a salue la position de Vladimir Poutine, qu'il considere comme un soutien aux revendications africaines en faveur d'une representation plus importante au sein des instances internationales. Il a egalement rappele que l'Union africaine avait adopte des resolutions appelant a une reforme rapide du Conseil de securite de l'ONU, afin que le continent puisse y occuper une place correspondant a son poids dans les affaires mondiales. Concernant la designation du prochain secretaire general des Nations unies, le president a exprime le souhait de voir l'Afrique presenter un candidat. Selon lui, cette eventuelle nomination constituerait une occasion a saisir pour le continent. En 2026, l'ONU choisira son dixieme secretaire general, qui succedera a António Guterres a compter du 1er janvier 2027. Sept candidats sont en lice, presentes par Antigua-et-Barbuda, l'Argentine, le Burundi, le Guyana, le Costa Rica, les Tonga et l'Ouganda. Le Conseil de securite procedera d'abord a un vote sur ces candidats. Une fois une candidature retenue, il la proposera a l'Assemblee generale pour approbation.

items.title: NRSA urges police to arrest pedestrians who fail to use footbridges
items.description: The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has urged the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service to arrest and prosecute pedestrians who fail to use designated footbridges, as part of efforts to reduce road crashes and fatalities. The Director-General of the NRSA, Abraham Amaliba, said strict enforcement of road traffic regulations was necessary to ensure pedestrian safety, particularly at locations where footbridges had been provided. “The footbridges are not there for decorative purposes; they are there for pedestrians to utilise them and be safe. If there is a footbridge and you decide not to use it and cross the road dangerously,” he said. “Where there are no footbridges, there will be no justification to arrest anyone, but where there are footbridges, and you refuse to use them, you must be prosecuted. I call on the police MTTD to start arresting and prosecuting people who refuse to use footbridges,” Mr Amaliba added. He made the call on October 28 at Madina Zongo in the La Nkwantanang-Madina Municipal Assembly during the launch of the Safe Crossing, Safe Lives pedestrian safety campaign. The campaign, an initiative of the Greater Accra Regional NRSA, seeks to promote safe pedestrian behaviour and encourage the proper use of footbridges and other designated crossing facilities to reduce pedestrian-related crashes and deaths. It targets high-risk locations in the Greater Accra Region, including Adentan, Madina, Lapaz and Weija. Mr Amaliba said the police MTTD must work with metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies (MMDAs) to enforce the use of footbridges and clear traders from pedestrian walkways to prevent pedestrian knockdowns. He stressed that road safety was a shared responsibility and said the NRSA was working with the police and other stakeholders to address road crashes. The call comes amid concerns about the increasing encroachment on road pavements and other infrastructure by traders and hawkers, which poses risks to pedestrians. According to the NRSA, pedestrian knockdowns account for 33 per cent of deaths from reported road crashes. Data cited in a Daily Graphic analysis of NRSA statistics show that 63,599 people died in road crashes across Ghana between 1991 and 2025, with about 20,988 of the deaths resulting from pedestrian knockdowns. The Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180), require pedestrians to use footbridges or underpasses where these have been provided. Regulation 154(3) states: “A pedestrian who fails to use a footbridge or an underpass where one is provided, commits an offence.” Regulation 154(10) further provides that a person who contravenes the regulation is liable, upon summary conviction, to a fine of not more than five penalty units, imprisonment for up to seven days, or both. Meanwhile, an Advanced Emergency Medical Technician at the National Ambulance Service (NAS), Dr Daniel Asare, has called for greater collaboration among stakeholders to prevent pedestrian knockdowns and other road crashes. He said road crashes not only resulted in the loss of lives but also had significant economic implications and placed additional pressure on the country’s emergency response system. Dr Asare acknowledged that government investment in ambulances had improved emergency response times compared with previous years, but said road crashes remained a major concern. “One severe pedestrian crash can take one ambulance for several hours from the scene to the hospital. “During that period, a pregnant woman in critical need of healthcare, a person with stroke, or a child with severe asthma has to wait with their life on the line for the next available ambulance,” he explained. He urged pedestrians to use footbridges, stressing that preventing crashes would help preserve emergency resources for other people in need. “What members of the public need to know is that footbridge use is better and safer than an ambulance; prevention is better than cure. When you cross safely, you are not only saving your life; you are saving the emergency response system for other people who need it to survive,” he said.

items.title: Sarkodie mourns Ghanaian teenager shot dead in New York
items.description: Ghanaian rapper Michael Owusu Addo, popularly known as Sarkodie, has expressed sorrow over the death of a Ghanaian teenager, Javits, who was reportedly shot in the abdomen while walking near a school in the Bronx, New York. The musician has also called for greater attention to parenting and the values instilled in children, saying the incident raises concerns about how young people are raised. In a Facebook post on Saturday, October 31, Sarkodie reflected on the upbringing of many Ghanaian children, saying he remained proud of the values instilled in them despite the country’s challenges. “We might have our difficulties here in Africa, especially in Ghana, but one thing I will always pride myself on is how we were brought up as children, even in rough and tough neighbourhoods,” he wrote. He said killings were generally treated as serious incidents in Ghana, attracting widespread media attention and leaving the public shocked and saddened. “Murder is a big deal out here. It’s almost alien to us because whenever something like that happens, it becomes major news. We announce and discuss almost every single case in the media, and as a people, we are always shocked and saddened by it,” he stated. Sarkodie also urged members of the Black community abroad to pay greater attention to parenting and the values they teach their children. “I honestly don’t know what kind of upbringing shapes children to become so evil. I think some of my fellow Black brothers and sisters out there need to do better when it comes to raising their children and instilling the right values in them,” he said. Read also: Ghanaian teen fatally shot while walking near Bronx school as police look for suspects He described Javits’ death as unfortunate and extended his condolences to the bereaved family, particularly the teenager’s parents. “It’s very unfortunate that we had to lose Javits this way. May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. Sending love, prayers and strength to the family, especially his mum and dad,” he wrote. He concluded his message by expressing his deepest sympathies to the family. “My deepest condolences,” he added.

items.title: Atlético beat Levante to move top above Barcelona
items.description: Atletico Madrid earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante on Saturday to move provisionally top of La Liga before Barcelona host Alaves later on. Diego Simeone’s side climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants, who suffered their first league defeat against rivals Real Madrid last weekend. Goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone in Valencia helped Atletico record a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. “I’m very happy with the team’s work,” Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. “We’re very far from the end of the season… we’ll keep going game by game.” There was a minute’s silence at the start of the match in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Levante’s Dani Requena forced Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak into an impressive early save. Morten Hjulmand thought he had put Atletico ahead after Alex Baena slipped him in, but a VAR review showed the Dane was offside. Baena, the visitors’ main creative outlet, was involved in the opener. The Spaniard’s pass was poorly defended by Levante and the ball bobbled through to Grimaldo, who lashed high into the net at the near post. Lee Kang-in hit the crossbar early in the second half as Atletico looked to put the game to bed. The coach’s son Giuliano prodded home for Atletico’s second goal after being played in by World Cup winner Baena. Oblak saved superbly from Karl Etta Eyong to stop the hosts fighting their way back into the game. It was Simeone’s 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club’s record set by Luis Aragones. “I don’t feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years,” said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga. On Sunday, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures. AFP The post Atlético beat Levante to move top above Barcelona appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sahara occidental : l’Algérie fustige un projet américain taillé « sur mesure » pour le Maroc
items.description: L’Algérie a exprimé son « profond regret » pour le non-renouvellement du mandat de la Mission des Nations Unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO), et exprimé des critiques à l’égard du projet de résolution américain, a réagi ce samedi le gouvernement algérien dans un communiqué. Vendredi, le projet de résolution américain pour le Sahara occidental et le renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso a été rejeté par le Conseil de sécurité à la suite du véto russe. Pour l’Algérie, la cause de cet échec est « l’excessive partialité » du projet de résolution américain et donc les États-Unis. L’Algérie dénonce un projet de résolution d’une « excessive partialité » « L’excessive partialité du projet de résolution soumis au Conseil de sécurité a rendu cette issue inéluctable. En effet, le projet penchait avec une telle outrance en faveur d’une partie, le Royaume du Maroc, au détriment de l’autre, le Front Polisario, qu’il ne pouvait prétendre sérieusement servir de base à une solution juste et durable du conflit du Sahara occidental », a critiqué le gouvernement algérien. Avant même la soumission du projet de résolution, le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Ahmed Attaf, a adressé des lettres officielles aux membres du Conseil de sécurité afin d’attirer leur attention sur les « conséquences particulièrement graves de l’évolution que connaissait le traitement du conflit du Sahara occidental ». M. Attaf a mis en garde les membres du Conseil contre les risques liés à l’adoption d’une résolution dont l’orientation tend à consacrer un « fait accompli territorial » et à « légitimer une situation d’occupation, au détriment du droit du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination », révèle le communiqué. En dépit des amendements introduits, la version finale du texte « vidait le droit à l’autodétermination de sa substance, en retenant le plan d’autonomie proposé par le Maroc, sous sa souveraineté revendiquée sur le Sahara occidental, comme unique base de négociation », déplore encore l’Algérie. La suppression du R de Minurso, un « signal politique préoccupant » Une telle approche « restreignait considérablement » les options ouvertes aux deux parties et préjugeait de l’issue du processus politique, alors même que le règlement du conflit devrait permettre au peuple sahraoui « d’exercer librement son droit à l’autodétermination », ajoute la même source. À cela s’ajoute la suppression dans le projet de résolution de la lettre « R », correspondant au terme « référendum », dans l’acronyme de la MINURSO, qui constituait un « signal politique préoccupant ». Cette suppression écartait a « priori l’option référendaire, pourtant historiquement associée au mandat de la Mission et à l’exercice du droit à l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui ». De même, et contrairement à l’approche retenue dans la résolution 2797, ledit projet privait le Front Polisario, reconnu comme représentant exclusif et légitime du peuple sahraoui, de la « possibilité de soumettre aux négociations ses propres idées » quant à une solution juste et durable du conflit au Sahara occidental, égrène le communiqué. « Le projet américain visait à transformer une question de décolonisation en problématique humanitaire » Pour l’Algérie, le projet de résolution américain préparait le terrain à une « transformation progressive » du conflit du Sahara occidental, d’une question de décolonisation en une « problématique essentiellement humanitaire, à laquelle il conviendrait de trouver des solutions durables ». « Or, en matière de décolonisation, une solution durable demeure indissociable de l’exercice, par le peuple concerné, de son droit inaliénable et imprescriptible à l’autodétermination », rappelle-t-elle. Pour conclure, l’Algérie estime que le projet de résolution américain « dénaturait » un processus de décolonisation, « légitimait l’acquisition d’un territoire par la force », « vidait » de sa substance et « privait » de son instrument le droit d’un peuple à l’autodétermination. Pour toutes ces raisons, « il ne pouvait pas valablement servir de cadre à des négociations productives tout comme il ne pouvait pas prétendre servir l’objectif de sécurité et de stabilité dans la région », assène encore le gouvernement algérien dans sa réaction. Enfin, l’Algérie réitère son attachement à une solution politique juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable, qui garantit au peuple sahraoui « l’exercice de son droit à l’autodétermination ». L’article Sahara occidental : l'Algérie fustige un projet américain taillé « sur mesure » pour le Maroc est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Immigration orders officers to eliminate delays, report cyber threats
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi As part of measures to ensure stronger customer service and tighter digital security, Comptroller General of Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nanna Nandap, has directed personnel to eliminate unnecessary delays in service delivery and to promptly report suspected cyber threats. Service Public Relations Officer, DCI Akinsola Akinlabi said Nandap gave the charge at two separate events in Abuja – the 2026 International Customer Service Week and the Service’s 2026 Cybersecurity Awareness Seminar. Speaking at the closing of the Customer Service Week, which ran from Wednesday, October 28, to Friday, October 30, under the theme “Going the Extra Mile – Creating a Lasting Smile,” Nandap urged officers to make excellent customer service part of the Service’s daily operations. She stressed professionalism, timely service delivery, prompt complaints resolutions and respectful treatment of customers. The Comptroller General charged officers to uphold integrity, eliminate unnecessary delays and make customer satisfaction a key performance benchmark. She also reaffirmed ongoing reforms to improve customer satisfaction and what the Service calls Hostmanship. The Head of Operations at the Service Compact with all Nigerians (SERVICOM) unit in the Presidency, Mrs Ngozi Akinbodewa, commended the Service for evolving its SERVICOM Unit. She said this year’s Customer Service Week marked a critical step towards sustaining citizen-focused service delivery in line with global best practices. Akinbodewa added that the international event offered an opportunity to recognise employees who go the extra mile in exceeding expectations and meeting customer needs. The Special Assistant to the Comptroller-General of Immigration Service on SERVICOM, DCI A.M. Abubakar, highlighted the importance of accountability, responsiveness and adherence to service standards. He urged officers to continually improve their conduct and prioritise customer satisfaction in the discharge of their duties. At the Cybersecurity Awareness Seminar, Nandap, who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller General, Finance and Accounts, DCG S.B. Daura, told officers that cybersecurity is a collective responsibility. She urged them to remain vigilant, observe established security protocols and promptly report suspected threats. She also called for continuous capacity building, institutional collaboration and proactive measures to address emerging cyber threats, before declaring the seminar open. Resource persons from the Department of State Services (DSS), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) made technical presentations. They covered inter-agency collaboration for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection, combating cybercrime through law enforcement and international cooperation, data protection and privacy in the digital age, and human risk management in the digital workplace. A plenary session facilitated by Galaxy Backbone Limited (GBB) examined strategies for securing critical systems through inter-agency collaboration, giving participants a chance to exchange experiences and explore practical approaches to strengthening the Service’s cybersecurity framework. The Service said the seminar reaffirmed its commitment to building a cyber-resilient institution through continuous capacity development, technology upgrades, inter-agency collaboration and compliance with global best practices. According to the statement, the initiative “underscores the Service’s resolve to protect its digital assets, secure sensitive information and strengthen its core mandates of Border Security and Migration Management in support of National Security.” The post Immigration orders officers to eliminate delays, report cyber threats appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La mayoría de las comisiones de los acampados en Sol se retira de la plaza para impulsar un movimiento social en los barrios
items.description: La mayoría de las comisiones que han permitido organizar durante más de un mes la acampada para reivindicar el derecho a la vivienda en Sol se han disuelto y sus integrantes han decidido abandonar el asentamiento, según un documento al que accedió este diario. La salida del núcleo duro de la concentración no es un punto y aparte, sino un punto y seguido: sus representantes aspiran a convertirse en un movimiento social que traslade su actividad a los barrios, concentrándose ahora en apoyar la huelga general del 11 de noviembre . Al tiempo, eso no quiere decir que las tiendas de campaña desaparezcan de Sol: permanece la comisión de Comunicación, y algunas personas de Cuidados, Pulmón y Cultura, según detalla Zahira Pagán, portavoz de quienes se han marchado. Además, también la asociación de personas sin hogar sigue presente. La explicación de las salidas está en el cumplimiento de parte de los objetivos de la concentración (poner en la agenda sus reivindicaciones) y en la advertencia de la Delegación del Gobierno sobre que “ podría resultar legítimo ponerle fin ”, tras un mes de respeto al derecho de reunión. Un doble aviso, a través de sendas comunicaciones enviadas el lunes y el jueves, que muchos no se han tomado a la ligera: unas 600 personas se han ido desde que se conoció, según Pagán. items.title: Inusah Fuseini says NPP’s suit on presidential term limit is needless
items.description: Former Tamale Central MP, Inusah Fuseini, says the New Patriotic Party (NPP) does not need to seek a Supreme Court interpretation of the constitutional provisions governing presidential term limits, arguing that the 1992 Constitution already provides a clear restriction. The lawyer maintains that Article 66(2) of the 1992 Constitution expressly limits an individual to two presidential terms, without distinguishing between consecutive and non-consecutive terms, making the NPP’s request for a judicial interpretation unnecessary. Mr Fuseini said the relevant constitutional provision was intended to limit the number of times a person could be elected to the presidency, rather than regulate how long they must stay out of office before seeking another term. “I think that the emphasis should actually be put on election, not the person,” he said in an interview on Channel One TV. To support his position, he drew a distinction between the presidency and Parliament, explaining that while the Constitution places a limit on presidential terms, it allows Members of Parliament to seek re-election without a prescribed limit. Mr Fuseini said he had personally served more than four terms as a legislator, a possibility he attributed to the absence of constitutional restrictions on the number of times an MP can be re-elected. He referred to Article 66(1), which sets the presidential tenure at four years, and Article 66(2), which states that a person “shall not be elected to hold office as President of Ghana for more than two terms”. “The Constitution is very clear. The drafters were very clear. They knew what they wanted. They wanted to impose term limits,” he said. For him, the wording of Article 66(2) leaves little room for a different interpretation, since it limits the number of times a person may be elected President without making a distinction between consecutive and non-consecutive terms. Mr Fuseini also took issue with the decision to involve the Supreme Court, arguing that the court cannot be called upon to rule on possibilities that have not materialised. “The Supreme Court has no speculative jurisdiction. It can’t speculate what anybody will do,” he said. He further raised concerns about the use of public resources to adjudicate a case based on a hypothetical situation, insisting that there must be an actual constitutional issue requiring the court’s determination. The NPP has instituted legal action against the Attorney-General, asking the Supreme Court to interpret Articles 58(2) and 66(1), (2) and (3)(a) of the 1992 Constitution. The party wants the Court to affirm that an individual cannot be elected President more than twice or occupy the position for more than eight years, whether the two terms are consecutive or separated by a period out of office.

items.title: Essaouira: 9 bus scolaires et 7 ambulance remises dans le cadre de l'INDH
items.description: Neuf bus de transport scolaire et sept ambulances ont été remis, samedi à Essaouira, au profit de plusieurs communes territoriales de la province, dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des programmes de l'Initiative Nationale pour le Développement Humain (INDH). S'inscrivant dans le cadre des activités commémorant le premier anniversaire de la Fête de l'Unité, cette cérémonie de remise des clés de bus de transport scolaire et des ambulances a été présidée par le gouverneur de la province d'Essaouira, Mohammed Rachid, en présence de chefs des services extérieurs, d'élus, de responsables des services sécuritaires et d'acteurs associatifs. Relevant des deuxième et quatrième programmes de la troisième phase de l'INDH, respectivement inhérents à l'Accompagnement des personnes en situation de précarité et à l'Impulsion du capital humain des générations montantes, ces opérations visent à renforcer l'offre de services de santé et d'éducation, ainsi qu'à faciliter l'accès aux prestations de base au profit des populations rurales, notamment dans les zones caractérisées par l'éloignement géographique des structures de santé. La remise des ambulances a bénéficié aux communes de Tahelouante, Assais et Bouzemmour, relevant du cercle d'Aït Daoud, d'Ait Aissi Ihahane et de Tidzi, relevant du cercle de Tamanar, ainsi que de Kechoula et de Sidi M'Hamed Ou Marzouq. Pour leur part, les neuf bus de transport scolaire ont été remis aux communes de Takoucht, relevant du cercle d'Aït Daoud, d'Ida Ou Guelloul, d'Imgrade, de Sidi El Jazouli et d'Imi N'tlit (cercle de Tamanar), de Zaouiat Ben Hmida, de Takate et de Had Draa (cercle d'Essaouira), ainsi que de Sidi Boulaalam, relevant du cercle d'El Hanchane. A cette occasion, les représentants des communes bénéficiaires ont salué cette initiative, qui « contribuera à améliorer les conditions d'accès aux soins de santé et à la scolarisation des populations locales, en particulier dans les zones rurales, tout en atténuant les contraintes liées à l'éloignement géographique et aux difficultés de déplacement ». Ils ont également souligné l'importance de ces équipements dans le renforcement des infrastructures de proximité et l'amélioration des conditions de vie des habitants, notamment les élèves et les personnes nécessitant une prise en charge sanitaire, mettant en avant le rôle crucial de l'INDH dans la promotion du développement humain et la réduction des disparités territoriales. A travers cette initiative, l'INDH poursuit son engagement sans faille au niveau de la province d'Essaouira, territoire à dominance rurale qui comprend 57 communes, en faveur de l'amélioration des conditions de vie des populations, du renforcement de l'accès aux services sociaux de base et de la promotion d'un développement territorial plus équitable et inclusif. items.title: Inusah Fuseini urges Mahama to reject 3rd term bid even if Supreme Court allows it
items.description: Former Tamale Central MP, Inusah Fuseini, has called on President John Dramani Mahama to reject any pressure to seek a third presidential term, even if the Supreme Court interprets the 1992 Constitution to allow such a possibility. He cautioned that attempts by African leaders who alter or manipulate constitutional provisions to prolong their stay in power have contributed to political instability and undermined democratic governance across the continent. Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, October 31, Mr Fuseini said respect for constitutional term limits should take precedence, regardless of the Supreme Court’s eventual decision on the matter. He expressed the hope that President Mahama would not pursue another term if the court rules that the Constitution permits a president to serve beyond two terms. “Even if the Supreme Court would rule that a president can go more than two terms, I would pray that John Dramani doesn’t do that. “What has caused instability in African countries is the tinkering with the Constitution,” he warned. The comments come amid a legal challenge by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) at the Supreme Court, seeking clarification on the constitutional provisions governing presidential tenure. The party wants the Court to determine whether the two-term limit restricts an individual to a maximum of eight years in office, irrespective of whether the terms are consecutive or separated by a break. Mr Fuseini maintained that the Constitution already provides for a maximum of two presidential terms, arguing that Article 66(2) makes no distinction between consecutive and non-consecutive periods in office. Beyond the legal arguments, he said attempts to manipulate constitutional arrangements for political advantage pose a threat to democratic stability. He identified the alteration of constitutional provisions by presidents seeking to extend their tenure as one of the factors contributing to instability in some African countries. Mr Fuseini further warned that such attempts could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions, particularly the judiciary, by creating perceptions that court decisions are being influenced to favour political interests.

Guinée : payés à 550 000 GNF par mois, des contractuels temporaires réclament leur intégration à la fonction publique
items.description: Le Collectif des Contractuels Temporaires de Guinée (CCTG) réclame la régularisation de la situation administrative de ses membres, dont certains totalisent plus de quinze années de service au sein de l’administration publique. Lors d’un point de presse organisé ce samedi 31 octobre 2026 à la Bourse du Travail de Conakry, les responsables du collectif ont dénoncé leurs conditions salariales et sociales, tout en sollicitant l’intervention du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, pour leur intégration à la fonction publique. À travers cette sortie médiatique, le collectif entend attirer l’attention des autorités sur la situation de milliers de contractuels temporaires qui, malgré plusieurs années de service au sein de l’État, ne bénéficient toujours pas d’un statut professionnel stable. Selon les responsables du CCTG, l’ancienneté de certains agents varie entre cinq, dix, quinze ans, voire davantage. Ils affirment que leurs membres sont pourtant identifiés dans le Fichier unique de gestion administrative et de la solde (FUGAS). « Certains d’entre nous servent l’État depuis 5 ans, 10 ans, 15 ans et plus pour l’intérêt supérieur de la nation », souligne le collectif dans sa déclaration. Au-delà de la question de leur statut, les contractuels dénoncent également la faiblesse de leur rémunération et l’absence de mesures d’accompagnement social. Ils affirment percevoir seulement 550 000 francs guinéens par mois, sans primes, indemnités ni couverture sanitaire. « Un salaire dérisoire de 550 000 GNF par mois, viré dans les différentes banques du pays, sans prime, ni indemnité, ni couverture sanitaire, ni avantage social », déplore le CCTG. Pour faire entendre leurs revendications, les responsables du collectif indiquent avoir multiplié les démarches auprès des autorités compétentes. Des demandes d’audience ont notamment été adressées au ministre secrétaire général du Gouvernement, au ministre de la Modernisation de l’administration et de la Fonction publique, au ministre d’État conseiller principal du chef de l’État, au Premier ministre ainsi qu’au président de l’Assemblée nationale. Toutefois, le collectif affirme que ces différentes sollicitations sont restées sans suite concrète. Les contractuels temporaires demandent désormais leur intégration à la fonction publique par voie d’arrêté ministériel. Ils estiment que leur expérience professionnelle et leur connaissance du fonctionnement des services administratifs constituent des arguments suffisants pour justifier cette régularisation. « Depuis plus de 10 ans, nous sommes au service de l’Administration publique et nous remplissons tous les critères qui ont conduit à notre enrôlement au Fichier unique de gestion administrative et de la solde (FUGAS). Nous avons l’expérience et nous maîtrisons l’Administration publique », soutiennent-ils. Le collectif déplore, par ailleurs, que des agents ayant consacré une grande partie de leur parcours professionnel à l’administration continuent d’être écartés des procédures de régularisation, notamment à l’occasion des concours de recrutement. « Comment pouvez-vous comprendre un jeune cadre au service de son Administration publique depuis plus de 10 ans avec 550 000 GNF toujours exclu de la régularisation de la situation administrative pendant le concours ? », s’interroge-t-il. Face à cette situation, le CCTG affirme vouloir privilégier les voies du dialogue et de la concertation. Dans cette perspective, il indique avoir saisi le Conseil national du dialogue social (CNDS), la Confédération nationale des travailleurs de Guinée (CNTG) et le Réseau des jeunes leaders (REJEL), dans l’espoir de faciliter une médiation avec les autorités. Les membres du collectif placent également leurs attentes dans les engagements du président Mamadi Doumbouya en faveur de la jeunesse et de la justice sociale. À leurs yeux, leur intégration dans les effectifs de la fonction publique représenterait une reconnaissance des services rendus à l’État. « La régularisation de la situation administrative des contractuels temporaires de l’Administration publique est un acte de justice sociale. Vous aviez invité cette jeunesse à abandonner le chemin de la Méditerranée et à se battre pour son avenir. Vous aviez promis que personne ne serait exclu et nous croyons à votre engagement », affirme le collectif. Dans son adresse au chef de l’État, le CCTG insiste sur la nécessité de mettre fin à cette situation qu’il juge injuste, en procédant à la transformation du statut de ses membres. « Nous adressons solennellement à Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi Doumbouya, président de la République, chef de l’État, notre cri de cœur pour transformer notre statut de contractuel temporaire en statut de fonctionnaire. C’est une réparation de justice sociale et de reconnaissance des services rendus à la nation », indique la déclaration signée par Thierno Bailo Diallo, coordonnateur national du CCTG. En attendant une réponse des autorités, le Collectif des Contractuels Temporaires de Guinée réaffirme sa volonté de poursuivre ses démarches dans un esprit pacifique et unitaire. Ses membres assurent rester mobilisés pour obtenir la régularisation de leur situation administrative et la reconnaissance de leurs années de service au sein de l’administration publique. items.title: Our part of Mbappe, China issue over – Real Madrid’s Mourinho
items.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday the club’s involvement in the controversy over Kylian Mbappe’s comments about an internet meme about himself and former Chinese leader Mao Zedong was over, after both the player and club apologised. Mbappe’s remarks sparked a backlash in China, with Real Madrid, the France forward and La Liga all issuing apologies, but Chinese state television nevertheless pulled Spanish football from its schedules. In a clip from an interview with French show “The Bridge” which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Mourinho said both Mbappe and 15-time European champions Real Madrid “had the class” to issue swift apologies and believes there is nothing more for them to do. “I’ve seen a lot of responsibility from a club which, at this level, is a club of great class, and as far as we’re concerned, that’s it, we’ve done our part, there’s nothing more for us to do,” Mourinho told reporters. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China, and the 27-year-old’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. “With this situation involving China, these are the dangers of today’s world, where many times the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, because there’s danger in so many things you say or comment on,” said Mourinho. Mbappe has endured a difficult week, after he finished second behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony. Mourinho praised Mbappe’s reaction after England international Kane was named the world’s best player. “Kylian is very intelligent, very mature, with a very high level of self-esteem,” said Mourinho. “At the same time, he shows real class in the way he’s interpreted the Ballon d’Or going to Harry. In him I’ve only seen and felt class and respect. “One thing is knowing you’re the best, and another is having respect for those who have also done a lot to win a trophy. From him I only see class.” Mourinho said midfielder Jude Bellingham coming in 11th in the voting left him with his “mouth open”, implying the Englishman should have finished far higher. However, the veteran Portuguese coach, who worked with Kane at Tottenham between 2019 and 2021, said he was happy for the Bayern hitman. “I had the privilege of working with Harry, he’s a great player and a great professional and a great person,” added Mourinho. “Inside the frustration that my player (Mbappe) didn’t win, well, I have to be honest and say I’m very happy for Harry, a player and a boy who deserves it.” The post Our part of Mbappe, China issue over – Real Madrid’s Mourinho appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Election Lies Are Already Starting on X
items.description: Last weekend, Chaya Raichik, the popular right-wing influencer who goes by Libs of TikTok, made an ominous claim to her nearly 5 million followers on X. “In Minnesota, the USPS offices are inside mosques,” she wrote. “The people who handle mail-in ballots.. What are we doing America.” She reshared a 28-minute-long video of a man circling a brick building in Plymouth, Minnesota, and accosting postal workers inside. “It’s the Islamification of the United States,” the man says. “And we have to stop it.” Almost everything about Raichik’s post is misleading. The post office is not “inside” a mosque; they are housed in different sections of the same building. And there’s no reason to believe that the shared real estate has anything to do with the integrity of elections. In situations like this, X’s crowdsourced fact-checking feature, called “Community Notes,” is supposed to help correct the record. Users propose disclaimers for popular posts they believe are inaccurate, and if other users agree, the disclaimer gets attached to the post. Sure enough, the day after Raichik’s post, someone suggested slapping the post with a Community Note to clarify the facts, citing and linking to articles by The Minnesota Star Tribune and Minnesota Public Radio. But the note was never publicly shown on X. As of yesterday, the video had more than 1.7 million views. (Raichik did not respond to a request for comment.) Since Elon Musk bought X four years ago, the platform has been a petri dish for rumors and propaganda. Now, having weathered a liberal exodus to other platforms, X could play a central role in the midterm elections—especially if Republicans fare poorly . X has become the go-to place for MAGA supporters to hunt for examples of voter fraud, which could be used to cast doubt on results that don’t go Republicans’ way. President Trump has endorsed this crusade—he recently announced a $1 million bounty for voter-fraud tips that lead to a conviction. Community Notes, which even some of Musk’s critics have praised as a worthwhile program, would seem to offer a bulwark against bogus claims of vote-rigging. It’s built around a clever idea: Each proposed note gets rated “helpful” or “not helpful” by users who have disagreed about related past notes. X publishes only the notes on which the users have reached a consensus. Yet even though X has expanded the feature, bringing in AI note writers to work alongside the human volunteers, it’s proving stubbornly incapable of addressing most election-related falsehoods. If Tuesday and the days afterward bring widespread claims of rigged results, expect many of them to originate on X. Since Musk embraced Community Notes on X, crowdsourced fact-checks have gone from a niche experiment to the default on social media. After Trump’s reelection, Meta ditched its partnerships with professional fact-checking organizations in the U.S. in favor of its own version of Community Notes. (Meta still uses professional fact-checks in other countries.) YouTube and TikTok have adopted similar features. But X’s version is the most established, and it has served as the industry’s model. In some respects, it works quite well: The system routinely corrects misleading posts about topics such as sports, pop culture, and advertising. [ Read: We’re back to the actually internet ] The problem is that it’s rare for liberals and conservatives to agree on notes that touch on the most polarizing topics—meaning that fact-checks about politics and elections rarely get approved. That has had predictable effects on the motivation of the program’s volunteers, Mike Doris, a longtime contributor to Community Notes, told me. A group chat where active members share information and sources has become a “ghost town,” Doris said. Some have given up; he is close to doing the same. While humans might get discouraged, bots do not. To scale up the program, X has opened fact-checking to AI, creating a purpose-built agent powered by Grok and inviting outside researchers to build AI fact-checking tools of their own. It might seem ironic that the same technology that can generate falsehoods at scale is now being used to catch them. Yet the bots are more prolific, and X says that notes proposed by AI are also more likely to win approval from the masses, perhaps because they’re trained to use neutral language and cite reputable sources. What started as an experiment last year has quickly become the norm: In May, an analysis by The Indicator ’s Alexios Mantzarlis found that half of all Community Notes shown on X are now written by just eight bot accounts. This month, the Georgetown University social-media researcher Renée DiResta analyzed X’s public research and found that six of those eight are controlled by the platform itself. This has led to a Cambrian explosion in the total number of Community Notes on X. But when it comes to politics, bots haven’t fixed the fundamental problem: Users on the left and the right just can’t find common ground. The proposed note for Raichik’s post about the post office attached to the mosque was, in fact, written by an AI agent, though not one of X’s. NewsGuard, a company that tracks misinformation, found that 93 percent of false claims about the midterms on X failed to receive a Community Note. (DiResta’s own AI fact-checking bot, she told me, has proposed 81 Community Notes; only one has been approved.) In the weeks before the election, many of these unchecked posts have involved false claims about candidates. Fake videos targeting at least three Democratic Senate candidates have been linked to Russian disinformation campaigns. One starts with a shot of a real Cleveland local-news reporter, then cuts to fabricated footage describing nonexistent claims of sexual misconduct against the Ohio Democrat Sherrod Brown by women who used to work for him. Darren Linvill, a Clemson University professor who researches foreign-interference campaigns, told me that X has taken down some of the accounts behind the posts, but the same group of influencers on the platform keeps amplifying new ones. Of the 37 viral false claims about the midterms identified by NewsGuard’s ongoing tracker, 22 started as X posts, and many of them spread to larger platforms from there. Not all of them target Democratic candidates: One debunked post claims that the Texas Republican Ken Paxton paid for a billboard that read, Pedos ain’t that bad . Fact-checks were never a cure-all for social-media lies. Many conservatives distrusted mainstream fact-checking organizations, and some research has shown that Community Notes are more broadly believed. A spokesperson for X told me that the addition of AI note writers has roughly doubled the number of Community Notes published in the past year. X, Meta, and other social-media companies also have rules against certain types of election misinformation, which they enforce through other means. For instance, X said earlier this month that it suspended more than 13,000 accounts linked to foreign-influence campaigns, and at least one viral post showing the satirical Paxton billboard now carries a “manipulated media” label. Still, the limits of crowdsourced fact-checking might become obvious in the days to come. AI bots in particular are likely to struggle to counter fast-flying fraud claims on Election Day, DiResta pointed out. “The AI does not know what is happening on the ground unless a human has written it somewhere retrievable,” she said. In 2020, the last national election when Trump was in the White House, the president’s claims that the election had been stolen gained traction on social media and helped fuel the Capitol insurrection on January 6, 2021. Back then, Twitter applied numerous fact-checks and warning labels to posts by Trump and his allies making unsupported claims that the vote had been rigged. It’s hard to envision the platform doing that this time around.

items.title: One dies, others injured in multiple accidents across Lagos
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, has cleared three overnight and early morning emergencies across the state, with one fatality recorded in Epe and two persons injured in three major incidents. According to reports, the first incident occurred at about 7:58pm on Friday on Odo-Iyalaro Bridge inward Maryland. Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Damilola Oke-Osanyintolu, said the operations reflect the commitment of the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration to prompt emergency response. The incident occurred when a Toyota Camry with registration number AGL-70HU and a Toyota Venza with registration number FST-893KF collided. Preliminary investigation revealed that the Venza had stopped by the roadside due to fuel insufficiency, while the driver of the Camry who was suspected to be under the influence of alcohol rammed into the stationary vehicle. Fortunately, no loss of life was recorded, however the driver of the Camry sustained injuries. He was stabilised by the agency’s paramedics and Lagos State Ambulance Service, LASAMBUS before being evacuated to the Trauma Centre for further care. Both vehicles were towed to Area F Police Station and the bridge reopened to traffic. Also at about 10:36pm, the Eagle Response Team responded to a broken down truck at Olosha, Mushin. The team discovered a HOWO truck with registration number JJJ-293XZ stuck due to a failed portion of the road, blocking about 60 percent of the carriageway. No casualty was recorded. Road diversion measures were put in place to manage traffic while before it was eventually towed away with the deployment of the agency’s heavy-duty equipment, restoring free vehicular movement. In the third incident, at about 6:19am on Saturday, the Whales Response Team stationed at Epe responded to a road traffic accident at Oke-Oso inward Itokin, Epe involving two tipper trucks loaded with granite. Investigation revealed that one of the trucks with registration number ABG-226XB suffered brake failure, lost control and had a side collision with another tipper. Sadly, the motor assistant of the first truck was thrown off the vehicle and died on impact and one other injured. The lifeless body was recovered, bagged and handed over to the Federal Road Safety Corps while both trucks were recovered and taken to the Federal Road Safety Commission, FRSC office. LASEMA commiserated with the family of the deceased and urged motorists to maintain their vehicles, avoid driving under the influence of alcohol and adhere strictly to road safety regulations. The agency assured residents of its readiness to respond to emergencies through its toll-free lines 767 and 112. The post One dies, others injured in multiple accidents across Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Première journée de la 18e édition du SIAO : la sécurité veille au grain
items.description: L’ouverture du parc d’exposition au public, à l’occasion de la 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), est intervenue le vendredi 30 octobre 2026 à 12h30, sur le site du salon. Pour cette première journée de la 18e édition du SIAO, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) sont fortement mobilisées. Leur mission consiste notamment à contrôler les visiteurs, à sécuriser le site et à assurer la protection des exposants et des participants. Leur vigilance a permis de saisir plusieurs objets, notamment des couteaux, des ciseaux, des briquets, des fonds de teint contenant des miroirs tranchants ainsi que des flacons de parfum. Certains appartenaient à des exposants, tandis que d’autres étaient détenus par des visiteurs, en dépit des consignes en vigueur. Dans une interview accordée aux Éditions Sidwaya, le président de la commission sécurité du SIAO, Aguima Abdoulaziz Yonli, par ailleurs directeur régional de la Police nationale du Kadiogo, a invité les usagers du site à respecter scrupuleusement les consignes données par les agents de sécurité. Il recommande notamment aux visiteurs d’éviter de venir avec des objets de grande valeur et de prendre les précautions nécessaires pour les protéger contre les vols. Les objets encombrants, susceptibles de gêner la circulation, sont également à éviter. « Leur travail vise à protéger les personnes et leurs biens », a-t-il rappelé. Toute personne constatant un comportement suspect ou une situation anormale est invitée à la signaler aux autorités compétentes. Selon lui, les numéros d’urgence à retenir sont le 10-10, le 17, le 18 et le 16. À l’endroit des exposants, Aguima Abdoulaziz Yonli a insisté sur le respect des consignes de prévention des incendies. « Les installations électriques anarchiques doivent être évitées, notamment les branchements improvisés destinés à alimenter des appareils ou à animer les stands », a-t-il prévenu. Selon lui, une harmonisation de la musique dans les pavillons est prévue afin de limiter les installations individuelles. Des consignes spécifiques ont également été données pour le village artisanal, notamment en matière d'installations électriques et de diffusion musicale. « La sécurité doit aller de pair avec l’hygiène publique, la salubrité et le respect des normes alimentaires. Une commission est chargée de ces aspects et nous apportons notre appui à la mise en œuvre des mesures prévues », a-t-il indiqué. Le respect de l’ensemble de ces consignes devrait permettre aux visiteurs, aux artisans et aux autres acteurs de prendre part au SIAO dans de meilleures conditions de sécurité. Wendaabo Cathérine KOURAOGO

items.title: Iran has no plans for talks with US — Foreign minister
items.description: Iran’s top diplomat on Saturday said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States despite growing concerns over a return to war. “Currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials, and any speculation to the contrary is merely media assumption,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA. “Under current circumstances, Iran sees no necessity for a meeting with the Americans; Iran’s conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators,” he said. Araghchi confirmed that Iran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, following days of diplomatic efforts to head off a return to violence. “The message from American Vice President JD Vance has been carefully reviewed and discussed in high-level meetings,” he said. “If Washington’s objective in sending the message is to sow discord, this would be yet another misstep, adding to America’s previous errors.” But Araghchi added: “The American side’s effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step.” AFP The post Iran has no plans for talks with US — Foreign minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Chelsea beat 10-man Manchester United to pile more pressure on Carrick
items.description: Chelsea took full advantage of Manchester United’s second-half collapse to condemn the visitors to a third straight loss and heap yet more pressure on Michael Carrick. United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988. A fourth Premier League defeat of the season leaves United 16th, a point above the relegation zone, with under-fire boss Carrick in an increasingly precarious position just days after being given the chance turn things around following a dismal start to the campaign. After an encouraging first-half performance, United allowed Morgan Rogers to saunter unchallenged through the heart of the defence to dink home the opener for Chelsea five minutes after the break. Cole Palmer doubled the hosts’ lead from the penalty spot 14 minutes later after the video assistant referee spotted Lisandro Martinez, not looking at the ball, thrust an arm into the face of Wesley Fofana. As a result, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow card and, once Palmer converted the spot kick, the game was all but over as a contest. It could have been worse for the away side as Chelsea winger Estevao, handed his first league start of the season by Xabi Alonso, smashed in a third, only for it to be ruled out for a marginal offside.

items.title: Chelsea beat Man Utd 2-0, push Carrick closer to exit
items.description: Michael Carrick’s stay of execution as Manchester United boss may not last long after his team imploded in a 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea on Saturday. The visitors wasted a string of chances to take the lead at Stamford Bridge before Morgan Rogers waltzed through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring on 50 minutes. Lisandro Martinez then ruined any chance of a revival from Carrick’s men with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty converted by Cole Palmer. Winless in nine games, defeat leaves the 20-time English champions still just one point above the relegation zone and in danger of ending the weekend in the bottom three. Many expected Carrick to be axed following last weekend’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth. The former United midfielder was instead given the chance to turn his side’s fortunes around and will lament a lack of ruthlessness during the first half. Carrick recalled captain Bruno Fernandes after he was left out last weekend in the wake of criticising his manager’s tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League. Fernandes should have marked his return with the opener when he blazed over from Bryan Mbeumo’s inviting cross. The roles were reversed when Mbeumo could not stretch to meet Fernandes’s delivery at the back post before twice Amad Diallo was denied by Chelsea’s stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders. United did finally get the ball in the net when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire’s header from a corner, but the Brazilian had strayed just offside. Carrick could not hide his frustration in a half-time interview to broadcasters and his mood soured further with a disastrous start to the second period. – Martinez sent off – Rogers credits Carrick for revitalising his career during a spell together at Middlesbrough but dealt a potentially decisive blow to his former boss. The England international collected the ball inside the centre circle but was allowed to drive directly towards the United goal before dinking the ball over Senne Lammens. Martinez also spoke out publicly in recent weeks to criticise United’s lack of spending in the transfer market to bolster Carrick’s squad. But on this season’s evidence, Martinez is one of those most in need of replacing. The Argentine international could not cope with Rogers’s strength moments later as he was penalised for hauling back the Chelsea forward. From the resulting free-kick, Martinez then needlessly crashed into Wesley Fofana with a raised forearm. After a VAR review, referee Peter Banks awarded a penalty and showed Martinez a second yellow card. Lammens got hands to Palmer’s spot-kick but still allowed the ball to trickle into the bottom corner. On a rare start since Xabi Alonso took charge of the Blues, Estevao had a third goal disallowed for offside when he crashed Palmer’s pass into the top corner. Cries of “sacked in the morning” rained down from the Chelsea fans as their side toyed with United for the final quarter without adding to their lead. Another big decision awaits the United hierarchy before a massive Champions League clash at home to Roma on Tuesday. Beaten in two of their three European games so far, United face both the embarrassment and financial shock of an early exit should they fall to another defeat against the Italians at Old Trafford. AFP The post Chelsea beat Man Utd 2-0, push Carrick closer to exit appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sindh CM Murad blames city planners for 'ruining' Karachi
items.description: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Saturday blamed urban planners for “ruining” Karachi, adding that he saw the metropolis vastly expand and deteriorate firsthand while growing up in it. In July 2025, a steering committee tasked with developing the Greater Karachi Regional Plan 2047 was informed that the new master plan of the country’s commercial capital would be ready within two years. Addressing an event of the Sindh Master Plan Authority (SMPA) in Karachi, CM Murad said: “Making a master plan from scratch is easy. But considering Karachi’s deteriorated condition, it is a challenge for consultants, master planners and urban developers to fix those [conditions], and also for the executive bodies to implement the plan.” CM Murad noted that SMPA , established under the Karachi Development Authority (KDA) in 1968, was formed to develop urban master plans for Sindh’s cities with recommendations from stakeholders. The chief minister said 14 master plans had been completed, but plans for Karachi and Hyderabad were under development. However, a post by the CM House quoted him as saying that master plans for 17 cities were complete, with work on 14 in final stages. Recalling that he grew up in Karachi and saw the metropolis’ expansion firsthand, Murad said, “I do not think any other city in the world has expanded as quickly as Karachi has, nor has any city in the world been ruined by planners as quickly as Karachi has.” The chief minister, whose PPP has ruled Sindh for about 15 years, stressed that Karachi needed to be improved. He contended that from the 1960s to the 1980s, it was a “very well-planned” city which attracted foreign visitors. Recalling an incident during the severe rains of 2020, Murad lamented that while travelling along a new dual-carriageway road from Yousuf Goth , he saw that people had set up shops along the side roads, the stormwater drains on either side of the main road and even on the median. “The planners did a very good job, but … a lot of roads have been declared commercial in the city and, to give people a livelihood, they are allowed to set up shops on stormwater drains for very cheap rent,” he said. “I request the help of all stakeholders in [solving] this issue. Unless the entire city comes together to make it better, then we will not be successful.” CM Murad also regretted that on several occasions, development work faced challenges due to delays from utility service providers, including the water board. He also pointed out the lack of mapping of utility infrastructure: “There is no mapping anywhere.” Noting Karachi’s population of 25 million and how urban development work inconveniences Karachiites, the chief minister said that funds have been arranged to rework 143 roads, but the work had not started because of procurement issues, which he said, “take a lifetime, but that’s how things are”. However, he stressed the importance of forums under SMPA to discuss urban planning and implementation. “These types of forums, seminars and discussions will help us bring some improvement and right now, in every city … the mayors and divisional headquarters are all trying to emulate the development which has started in Karachi.”

items.title: 37e Tour du Faso: l’Algérien Hamza Yacine remporte la 2e étape Ouagadougou-Koudougou
items.description: Le cycliste algérien Hamza Yacine a remporté, ce samedi 31 octobre 2026, la 2e étape du 37 e Tour du Faso courue entre Ouagadougou-Koudougou, une distance longue de 129,75 km. Son compatriote Assal Mohamed Nadib et le Burkinabè Paul Daumont complètent le podium de la course de ce jour. La deuxième étape du 37 e Tour du Faso s’est courue, ce samedi 31 octobre 2026, entre la capitale burkinabè et la ville de Koudougou. Longue de 129,75 km, cette compétition a enregistré au départ 78 coureurs avant que ne soit signalé deux abandons à l’issue de l’étape. Pour les résultats du 2e sprint intermédiaire à Sabou, le Burkinabè Idrissa Ouangraoua de l'équipe régionale du Centre est arrivé 1 er , suivi du deuxième, Issouf Ilboudo de l'équipe régionale de l'Ouest du Burkina Faso. L’Algérien Anes Riahi est arrivé troisième. Au premier sprint intermédiaire à Kokolgo, c’était Idrissa Ouangraoua qui arrivait en tête du peloton suivi toujours de Issouf Ilboudo et le Sud-africain, Emile de Tshenolo Van Niekerk se positionnait en troisième rang. Lors du sprint final de cette étape, Moussa Oumarou, meilleur coureur Camerounais le mieux classé, a été victime d'une chute. La première étape du Tour du Faso 2026 a été remportée hier vendredi par le Néerlandais Tom Wijfje. Elle a été courue sur 152,15 kilomètres entre Ouagadougou et Kaya. Le Burkinabè Souleymane Koné s’est illustré en terminant deuxième place. Addo was earning a monthly salary of $50,000 after signing a 34-month contract with the GFA in March 2024. items.title: Why You Must Read Morgenthau’s Politics Among Nations: A Note to African Peace and Security Researchers 1
items.description: The rise and dominance of the liberal peace thesis may have led many peace and security researchers to neglect the guardrails that Hans Morgenthau offered in his seminal book, Politics Among Nations: The Struggle for Power and Peace . Staying cognisant of those guardrails has become fundamental in our pursuit of peace in Africa. The liberal peace thesis contends that we can engineer peace by promoting and spreading liberal values. These include democracy, human rights, market economies, and international institutions. The assumption is that introducing these values in conflict-prone or conflict-affected societies will produce peace. This theory reached its peak prominence in the 1990s, after the end of the Cold War, and has since dominated key reference points in peace and security discourse. The liberal peace thesis has been the vehicle through which institutions such as the African Union (AU), Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and Regional Mechanisms advance their agenda for integration, peace, and stability. That is why these buzzwords will always sound familiar: democratic governance, rule of law and human rights, constitutionalism, free market and trade, strong international institutions, and statebuilding, among others. Subsequently, many researchers working on the African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA) have ploughed this path in search of ways to achieve sustainable peace in Africa. They are attempting to offer the much-needed intellectual support to the AU, RECs/RMs, and their member states. Various arguments have emerged that critique the premises and origins, approaches, and compatibility of the liberal peace thesis, some of which informed the hybrid and post-liberal peace ideas. Yet, the liberal peace thesis endures and continues to define the policy and programme design of APSA institutions, as well as their respective implementation approaches. The establishment of APSA institutions was largely premised on the ideas and interpretations of the liberal peace thesis, in relation to pressing peace and security issues on the continent. Conflict realities on the continent in the 1990s that drove the need to establish APSA, and in the 2000s, arguably APSA’s earliest formative years, coincided with the peak of the liberal peace thesis’s influence. At this juncture, it is important to recognise that the AU has operated in a hybrid space wherein its approach, beyond its overt engagements, often falls at the intersection of power politics and liberal ideas: a constant pressure worth acknowledging. The interaction between APSA and the liberal peace thesis was not merely coincidental. Examine the AU Constitutive Act, adopted on 11 July 2000 and entered into force on 26 May 2001; the Protocol Relating to the Establishment of the Peace and Security Council (PSC) of the African Union, adopted on 9 July 2002 and came into force on 26 December 2003; the Continental Early Warning System (CEWS); the Panel of the Wise (PoW); the African Charter on Democracy, Elections, and Governance (ACDEG), and some others. Their themes can be traced back to mitigating plans or solutions (to peace and security challenges), rooted in the liberal peace thesis that dominated intellectual and policy discourse around the time these documents came into being. Regardless, Morgenthau’s guardrail was clear. The power struggle cannot be divorced from domestic and international politics, even though their manifestations differ. Morgenthau argued for 3 basic observable patterns that may be adopted as analytical tools to guide thinking and questioning, without necessarily being a full steward of classical realism. These patterns are: keeping power, increasing power, and demonstrating power, and they apply at all levels of analysis and to state and non-state actors. In modern-day Africa, violent extremists in the Sahel often seek to increase and keep power for greater resources and leverage to confront African states. At the same time, they demonstrate it to instil fear towards citizens. In eastern DRC, while some armed groups seek to consolidate what they have to keep the flow of finances they derive from mining, others seek to challenge the status quo to increase it. The same goes for the highly fragmented armed non-state actors in Libya, particularly in the context of oil. These three patterns are also useful tools for understanding foreign policy dynamics among Horn of Africa and Nile Basin countries, primarily involving Ethiopia, Egypt, Sudan, Somalia, Eritrea, and Gulf countries. Overall, failing to identify which pattern is at play poses a risk of designing incomplete interventions or interventions that are not fit-for-purpose altogether. Morgenthau names these patterns as follows: the policy of status quo, the policy of imperialism, and the policy of prestige. He further offers how to detect them and warns about the dangers of misanalysis. Unfortunately, many researchers miss the point and engage in their analyses and policy recommendations without due consideration of this critical element. For state actors, misanalysis may lead to foreign policy failure or inefficiency. For non-state actors such as civil society organisations (CSOs) and International Non-Governmental Organisations (INGOs), misanalysis will prevent them from accurately assessing their limits and leverage relative to other actors. For intervening actors in peace and security contexts, misanalysis makes it more difficult to understand what drives conflict actors and their methods, as well as where they are least opposed to a peaceful resolution. Misanalysis may precipitate impasses, conflict re-escalation, failed negotiations or agreements, or the entrenchment of historical injustices, among other outcomes. On this note, Morgenthau emphasises the need to accurately distinguish among those who seek to maintain the power structure, upset it to their advantage, or demonstrate it (sometimes to serve the first two). How we assess the actors in a conflict-intervention dynamic constitutes a significant portion of what we recommend and the approaches we propose to implement those recommendations. Our misanalysis may therefore be the difference between prevention and outbreak, or resolution and escalation. Ergo, avoiding misanalysis of which actor(s) seek to maintain, increase, or demonstrate power is imperative if our work is to equip policy- and decision-makers to effectively confront the daunting realities they face during peace efforts. The liberal peace approach has undoubtedly done substantial good for humanity. However, fixation on peace solely through the lens of the liberal peace thesis may constitute a fundamental flaw that Morgenthau warned against: actor misanalysis. Thus, while the liberal peace thesis has brought us closer to sustainable peace, the guardrails Morgenthau offers must not be ignored. Morgenthau focused on military, economic, and cultural dimensions, and largely on inter-state relations. However, modern realities dictate that we must account for the digital dimension, as it is inevitable to ignore the advantages the digital advancements offer armed actors in the context of armed conflicts. Our assessments must also include non-state actors. Disclaimer: The views expressed in this Insight reflect the perspectives of the contributor and do not necessarily represent the official position of Institute for Peace and Security Studies. Contributed by Jesutimilehin O. items.title: Sahara marocain : le double veto, point d’inflexion
items.description: Le veto russe au projet de résolution américain, puis celui de Washington au contre-projet de Moscou, laissent la Minurso sans reconduction de son mandat. Le dossier quitte ainsi la logique de gestion du différend pour entrer dans une dynamique de résolution défintive, autour de l’initiative d’autonomie. Le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies n’a adopté, vendredi 30 octobre, aucun des deux projets de résolution soumis à son vote sur le Sahara marocain. Le texte américain a recueilli onze voix pour et trois abstentions, mais la Russie s’y est opposée par son veto. Le projet russe, qui visait à recondure le mandat de la mission onusienne pour un an sans changement de nom ni de prérogatives, n’a obtenu que trois voix et s’est heurté au veto des États-Unis. Sans texte adopté, le mandat de la mission expire le 31 octobre. Le Cabinet royal a aussitôt vu dans cette non-reconduction un pas significatif vers la clôture du dossier aux Nations unies. Il a jugé le processus onusien suspendu, tout en réaffirmant l’attachement du Royaume au cessez-le-feu. Au-delà de l’épisode procédural, ce double veto accélère une dynamique historique : celle d’un dossier qui s’organise autour de l’autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine, érigée en cadre de référence de la légitimité internationale, et dont les prochaines heures doivent préciser les équilibres. De la gestion conjoncturelle à la décantation structurelle Contacté par Hespress FR, Azzeddine Hannoun, professeur de droit public à la faculté des sciences juridiques et politiques de l’université Ibn Tofaïl, revient sur ce tournant diplomatique. Il relève qu’il met en évidence une véritable accélération de la dynamique historique autour de la question du Sahara marocain, et que les prochaines heures s’annoncent particulièrement décisives pour acter les équilibres géopolitiques en cours. « Sur le plan de l’analyse des relations internationales, nous assistons à un passage progressif d’une logique de gestion de conflit à une dynamique de résolution structurelle » , observe-t-il. « L’initiative d’autonomie présentée par le Royaume s’est imposée durablement comme le cadre de référence et le dénominateur commun de la légitimité internationale. Cette accélération de l’histoire reflète la convergence entre la constance de la diplomatie marocaine et l’évolution pragmatique des positions des grands acteurs internationaux », affirme M. Hannoun. S’agissant de l’enjeu des prochaines heures, le professeur de droit public souligne que « les développements observés hier marquent un point d’inflexion méthodologique et politique » . « Les prochaines heures seront déterminantes dans la mesure où elles cristallisent un ensemble de mutations de fond » , poursuit-il. « Elles exigeront de l’ensemble des parties prenantes et des instances multilatérales une lecture lucide de la réalité géopolitique régionale, confirmant l’irréversibilité de la dynamique impulsée par le Maroc en faveur de la stabilité et du développement de la région ». Pour Azzeddine Hannoun, la démarche marocaine est aussi une haute expression de réalisme. « Sur le plan théorique, la démarche du Maroc constitue une illustration probante de ce que les relations internationales qualifient de “réalisme politique” (ou realpolitik) » , explique-t-il. « L’initiative d’autonomie ne relève pas d’une posture doctrinale figée, mais procède d’une lecture pragmatique des réalités du terrain et des impératifs de sécurité régionale. En proposant une solution de compromis réaliste et viable, le Royaume a su faire prévaloir la stabilité géopolitique globale sur des schémas abstraits ou dépassés » . Et d’ajouter : « c’est précisément cette maturité stratégique qui explique aujourd’hui l’adhésion croissante de la communauté internationale et l’accélération observée dans la résolution de ce dossier ». The post Sahara marocain : le double veto, point d’inflexion appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Dori : La prison à vie pour un homme qui a versé de l’acide sur le visage de sa copine enceinte
items.description: La chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dori a condamné un homme, le 30 octobre 2026, à la « réclusion criminelle à perpétuité ». Il a été reconnu coupable d'avoir agressé sa copine enceinte à l'acide et au couteau, selon un communiqué du parquet publié le même jour. Les faits remontent à la nuit du 31 août 2026, selon le communiqué. Le 1 er septembre 2026, le commissariat central de police de Dori informe le parquet qu'une jeune femme a été retrouvée « grièvement blessée au visage et inconsciente » à Torodi, un village situé à une dizaine de kilomètres de la ville. Elle est conduite au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Dori, et une enquête est ouverte. Agressée pour avoir refusé d'avorter La victime présente des « brûlures graves » au visage, à la poitrine et aux mains, ainsi que des blessures sur l'ensemble du corps. Selon le parquet, elles auraient été causées par de « l'acide et un objet contondant (couteau ) ». Sa famille est retrouvée trois jours plus tard grâce à un communiqué administratif. Après avoir repris conscience, la jeune femme désigne son « copain » comme l'auteur des faits. Elle était enceinte de lui et avait refusé « une interruption volontaire de la grossesse ». Il aurait alors « usé de stratagèmes » pour l’emmener de nuit dans « un coin reculé ». Là, il l'a battue, l'a blessée au dos avec un couteau, puis lui a versé de l'acide sur le visage, « la défigurant complètement ». Il l'a abandonnée inconsciente sur place. Elle n'a été secourue qu'« in extremis » le lendemain matin. La prison à vie « Grâce à la collaboration des populations », le suspect est interpellé le 15 octobre 2026. Le 20 octobre, il est déféré au parquet et placé sous mandat de dépôt. Il est poursuivi pour « coups et blessures volontaires criminels », en vertu de l'article 512-22 du Code pénal. Dix jours plus tard, la chambre criminelle le reconnaît coupable. Il est condamné à la « réclusion criminelle à perpétuité ». Le parquet salue « le professionnalisme et l'abnégation » du personnel soignant du CHR de Dori, qui a sauvé la vie de la victime. Il félicite aussi l'unité de police judiciaire et la population pour sa « franche collaboration ». items.title: COCOBOD CEO woos investors with Ghana’s new cocoa financing model at New York forum
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), Dr Ransford Anertey Abbey, has presented Ghana’s new cocoa financing model and outlined reforms aimed at strengthening the cocoa sector at the Africa Cocoa Finance & Investment Forum (ACFIF) in New York. Speaking at the forum on Monday, Dr Abbey highlighted measures designed to improve farmer incomes, attract investment, expand domestic cocoa processing and build a more resilient cocoa economy. He also invited investors to explore opportunities in Ghana’s cocoa industry, drawing attention to the government’s policy target of processing 50 per cent of the country’s cocoa beans locally. The COCOBOD Chief Executive also highlighted investment opportunities in cocoa processing, sustainability, traceability, farm rehabilitation and value addition, urging investors to partner with Ghana in developing these areas. The presentation comes as Ghana rolls out a new cocoa financing framework anchored by Cocoa Capital PLC, which is raising GH¢16.3 billion through a domestic securities programme to finance cocoa purchases and address legacy debt obligations. The initiative, according to COCOBOD, is expected to reduce reliance on the traditional offshore syndicated loan arrangement and mobilise domestic capital for the sector.
